facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: CSAM orchestration is making the customer-success system observable enough to run.
keyTalkingPoints: Handoffs need an input, owner and date. Escalation is not a failure when it is used to unblock the system and protect customer outcomes.
discussionQuestions: Where does work currently stop between Microsoft, the partner, and the customer?
Who believes they own something that someone else also believes they own?
Which handoff have you personally been compensating for?
suggestedTransitions: Move from the coordination map to the one handoff you will make explicit, with both sides named.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Name the handoff you will make explicit, both parties by name, and the date it will be agreed rather than assumed.
preparationChecklist: Before the session: bring one workstream involving Microsoft, customer, partner, support or delivery handoffs.
facilitatorQuestions: Where exactly does work stop between the three parties?
Who thinks they own that step, and have you asked them?
What are you personally absorbing because the handoff does not work?
listenFor: Listen for the CSAM compensating for a broken handoff rather than fixing it, ownership assumed across company boundaries, partner commitments with no date, and coordination meetings that report rather than decide. Also listen for the customer's own team being left out of the orchestration picture.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the tool or data source is unavailable, map the current workflow manually, name the trusted sources and draft the prompt plus human checkpoint for later testing.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Make one handoff explicit this week by agreeing it with both sides rather than assuming it.
bringBackEvidence: Bring the handoff, both owners, and the date it was agreed.

secondaryAgents.name: Sales Home
secondaryAgents.shortDescription: The seller landing surface inside Sales Agent, opened from Microsoft 365 Copilot. It brings your alerts and quota attainment, your prospecting signals and your pipeline into one place, and answers questions against what MSX holds. It is in preview for SME&C sellers on MSX and is enabled for individual contributors, not managers.
secondaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Pull the real state of an opportunity out of MSX and read it back plainly: the current stage and when it last moved, the recorded next step and who owns it, the close date and what supports it, and any blocker or objection captured against the account. It works across your whole book, so you can ask which opportunities in your solution area have a named competitor recorded, which partners keep letting co-sell records lapse, or which accounts already carry a discount or non-standard term. It also drafts first-touch outreach to contacts that already exist in MSX, in English.
secondaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Use it when the question is what is on the record. Deal preparation, pressure-testing a close date, working your prospecting signals, checking the concessions already in force on an account before you negotiate, or finding the other opportunities where this same objection has already come up. Reach for it first whenever you would otherwise open MSX and click through an opportunity by hand. If Sales Home has not been turned on for you, Sales Accelerator covers the same prospecting and signal work and is where your queue lives. Sales Agent is the wider conversational surface that Sales Home sits inside, so if you are already in a Sales Agent chat you do not need to switch.
keyBenefits: Replaces the click-through: stage, next step, owner, close date and open objection come back in one answer instead of four screens in MSX. Because it reads across your whole book at once, questions that used to mean opening opportunities one at a time, such as where a competitor has shown up, which partners keep lapsing, or what you have already conceded on an account, become a single prompt. Most usefully, it shows you where the record is empty, which is normally the thing costing you the deal.

resources.description: Turns engagement notes into a shareable case study with customer-identifying detail removed.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Adoption activity does not automatically become customer value. Today is about proving and accelerating value realization.
keyTalkingPoints: Adoption plans should link underused features, customer priorities, behavior-change actions, milestones and value evidence. AI can draft the plan and value narrative; the CSAM validates truth and relevance.
discussionQuestions: What value has this customer actually realized that you could prove today?
Where is adoption stalled, and do you know why or are you guessing?
What would the customer say they got, if asked without us in the room?
suggestedTransitions: Move from the value picture to one claim you will evidence, and one adoption barrier you will actually diagnose.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Name one value claim you will evidence, one adoption barrier you will diagnose rather than guess at, and how you will say it back to the customer.
preparationChecklist: Before the session: bring one workload or solution where adoption progress, friction or value proof needs to be clarified.
facilitatorQuestions: What value can you evidence today, and what are you asserting?
Where adoption stalled, do you know the cause or are you inferring it?
Would the customer describe the value the same way you just did?
listenFor: Listen for value claimed from usage figures alone, adoption barriers guessed rather than investigated, realized value described in Microsoft terms rather than customer outcomes, and proof that would not survive a procurement conversation. Also listen for value stories that have never been said back to the customer.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the tool or data source is unavailable, map the current workflow manually, name the trusted sources and draft the prompt plus human checkpoint for later testing.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Evidence one value claim, and diagnose one adoption barrier instead of guessing at it.
bringBackEvidence: Bring the evidenced claim and what you found was actually blocking adoption.

CSAM-VALUE.keyTakeaway: Value that is not evidenced is an opinion. Value that is not communicated is invisible.

agents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Renewal readiness starts before the renewal motion. Today is about seeing risk and growth conditions early.
keyTalkingPoints: Consumption, MACC or usage trajectory, adoption gaps, value evidence, support health and stakeholder signals all shape renewal confidence.
discussionQuestions: Which renewal are you least confident about, and what specifically drives that?
What consumption signal would you want to see six months before a renewal conversation?
Where is growth genuinely available versus where are you hoping?
suggestedTransitions: Move from the forecast to the one early signal you will start tracking, and who you will align it with.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Name the renewal you are least confident about, the early signal you will start tracking, and who you will align the forecast with.
preparationChecklist: Before the session: bring one account with renewal, consumption, usage or expansion relevance in the near planning horizon.
facilitatorQuestions: What is your forecast based on, and how far ahead does the signal reach?
Which growth opportunity is supported by consumption evidence?
What would you need to know now to avoid a surprise at renewal?
listenFor: Listen for forecasts driven by relationship confidence rather than consumption evidence, growth assumed from headroom rather than intent, renewal risk surfacing late because nobody looked early, and commercial ownership blurring between CSAM and CE. Also listen for consumption trends read without seasonality.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the tool or data source is unavailable, map the current workflow manually, name the trusted sources and draft the prompt plus human checkpoint for later testing.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Start tracking one early consumption signal and hand it to the account owner.
bringBackEvidence: Bring the signal, why it matters, and who you handed it to.

activities.prompt: Use Agent J.ai to role-play the customer stakeholder I have to tell about this escalation. Use the approved status position, the validated escalation brief and the commitment boundaries I am pasting below, and ask me for anything missing before you begin. Play them as someone who is frustrated and wants a date I cannot yet give. Push back where I over-commit, where I soften the impact, or where I explain the cause instead of saying what happens next. Pause for my response before coaching me on whether I was clear about what is known, what is not, and when they will hear from me again. Do not invent facts about the incident.

activities.requiredContext: The validated escalation brief; the stakeholder and what they care about; the approved communication position; what you cannot yet commit to.
activities.whyThisMatters: How an escalation is handled shapes the relationship long after the incident closes. Rehearsing it is cheaper than improvising it while they are angry.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Escalations test trust. Today is about moving from scattered status to a grounded recovery plan.
keyTalkingPoints: A useful brief names customer impact, current status, owner, decision needed, next action and update cadence. AI can consolidate threads; the CSAM validates tone, accuracy and accountability.
discussionQuestions: What issue are you currently managing that should probably already be escalated?
What is holding you back: evidence, ownership, or the conversation itself?
When an escalation last worked well, what made it work?
suggestedTransitions: Move from the delivery risk to a recovery plan with an owner, a customer message, and a defined exit condition.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Name the risk you will escalate or resolve this week, the recovery commitment delivery can actually support, and what the customer will be told.
preparationChecklist: Before the session: bring one live or recent delivery risk, incident, support issue or overdue commitment.
facilitatorQuestions: What threshold would have told you to escalate this a month ago?
What does the recovery plan commit us to, and can we deliver it?
What will you tell the customer, and when?
listenFor: Listen for escalation delayed to avoid an uncomfortable conversation, recovery plans that promise more than delivery can support, customer communication planned after the internal fix rather than alongside it, and escalations raised without a defined exit. Also listen for the same issue recurring without anyone treating the pattern.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the tool or data source is unavailable, map the current workflow manually, name the trusted sources and draft the prompt plus human checkpoint for later testing.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did you learn today? Name one thing AI made easier, one thing that still needed your judgment, and one thing you would do differently next time.
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Take one issue to escalation or resolution this week, with a recovery commitment delivery can actually support.
bringBackEvidence: Bring the issue, the recovery plan, and what the customer was told.

DAE-SIGNAL.name: Work the Signal Queue Before It Expires
DAE-SIGNAL.description: Take an inbound queue of marketing signals and plan priorities, decide fast which ones are real, and act on them inside the window rather than after it.
DAE-SIGNAL.todayObjective: Triage your current signal queue, action the one closest to expiry, and record a decision on the ones you are letting go.
DAE-SIGNAL.whyItMatters: Signals arrive faster than anyone can work them, and the ones that expire do so silently. Whoever is deliberate about which signals they drop ends up ahead of whoever tries to work them all.
DAE-SIGNAL.desiredOutcome: A triaged queue with expiring signals identified, one signal actioned, and an explicit decision on everything you are not pursuing.

activities.name: See what is in your queue and what is closest to expiring
activities.description: Read your open signals and plan priorities out of the tool, then work out which ones the clock has almost run out on.
activities.prompt: Here are the open signals and plan priorities in my queue: [paste the list from the tool, with the type and arrival date of each]. The windows that apply are 48 hours for a Contact Me signal, 5 days for Highly Engaged, and 14 days for a preloaded Plan Priority. Work out from the arrival dates which are already past their window, which are closest to it, and which I have not given you enough information to judge. Order them by time remaining rather than by account size. Do not tell me which to pursue yet; I need the clock first.
activities.expectedOutput: Your signals ordered by time remaining against the applicable windows, with anything already overdue named and anything you could not date flagged.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE decides what the queue actually means. The ordering is arithmetic, but only you know that a large account with a weak signal may still be worth more of your week than three small ones about to expire.
activities.requiredContext: Access to Sales Home or Sales Accelerator; your open signals and preloaded plan priorities with their arrival dates; the SLA windows that apply to you.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Home and go to the Prospecting section, or Sales Accelerator if Sales Home is not enabled for you. Sales Home is in preview and has only been enabled for individual contributors, not managers.
2. Read the Signals Overdue, Actioned and New this week figures. Those come from the tool and are the reliable numbers.
3. Copy your open signals and priorities into the prompt where it asks, with the type and arrival date of each, then run it.
4. Start with anything already past its window. Those are decisions you have already made by not making them.
5. Pick the signal closest to expiring that you have not yet looked at properly. That is the one you will work next.
activities.whyThisMatters: Signals expire silently. Sorting by what is closest to gone, rather than by what looks most interesting, is the single habit that changes how many of them you keep.

activities.name: Find out who this account is before you contact anyone
activities.description: Build enough of a picture of the account behind a signal to make the first contact worth the customer's time.
activities.prompt: I have an inbound signal from [account name or TPID] and a short window to act on it. Give me what I need before I make contact: what this company does, what they already have from us, anything recent that would explain why they engaged now, and who the plausible contacts are. Tell me which of this you can actually see and which I would have to find elsewhere. Treat the signal as an unqualified lead, not as intent, and do not write me an outreach message yet.
activities.expectedOutput: A short account picture covering what they do, what they already have, what changed recently, and plausible contacts, with the gaps you would need to fill elsewhere named.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE confirms the signal is worth acting on before contacting the customer. Signals are unqualified leads until confirmed, and a contact made on a weak signal costs credibility you will need later on that account.
activities.requiredContext: One signal and its account or TPID; access to account and consumption history; the ability to check whether a contact exists in MSX.
activitySteps: 1. Take the signal you selected in the previous practice.
2. Replace the bracketed placeholders in the prompt with your own details, then run it.
3. Look for the reason they engaged now. That is what makes a first contact land rather than sound generic.
4. Check the contact actually exists in MSX. Sales Home cannot draft an email to someone who is not in the system.
5. Decide whether this is worth a real contact attempt. If the answer is no, say so now rather than after you have written the email.
activities.whyThisMatters: Most first contacts on a signal fail because they are generic. The difference is knowing what changed at that company recently, which takes minutes to find and is obvious to the customer when it is missing.

activities.name: Take a plan priority to a decision rather than letting it sit
activities.description: Move a preloaded plan priority to a real outcome, either converted into an opportunity or closed with a reason.
activities.prompt: Here is a preloaded plan priority I own: [paste the priority, the account, what the system suggested and what I know about the account]. Help me decide the honest next step. Is there enough here to convert it into a Stage 1 opportunity, is there something specific I need to confirm first, or should it be closed? For each option, tell me what evidence supports it. If you think it should be closed, say so plainly rather than suggesting more research. Where I have not given you something you need, ask me for it instead of assuming.
activities.expectedOutput: A recommended next step of convert, confirm-first or close, with the evidence for each option and the specific thing to confirm if that is the recommendation.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE owns the decision to convert or close. A model working from the record cannot know the account context that makes an unpromising-looking priority worth pursuing, or a promising one already dead.
activities.requiredContext: A preloaded plan priority you own; what the system suggested; what you know about the account; access to MSX to convert or close it.
activitySteps: 1. Take a preloaded plan priority you own, ideally one that has been sitting.
2. Paste what you know into the prompt where it asks, then run it.
3. Answer whatever it asks rather than letting it fill the gap itself.
4. Take the decision. Converting it to an opportunity and closing it with a reason are both good outcomes; leaving it open is the only bad one.
5. Record why. A closed priority with a reason is evidence for the next planning cycle; one that just expired is nothing.
activities.whyThisMatters: Preloaded priorities are generated for you, which makes them easy to ignore. The ones that expire without a decision teach the system nothing and cost you the coverage.

activities.name: Find the pattern in what you keep letting go
activities.description: Look back at the signals you did not action and work out whether you were triaging deliberately or simply running out of time.
activities.prompt: Here are the signals and plan priorities I did not action recently: [paste the list, with the type, account, and whether I declined it deliberately or never reached it]. Group them and tell me what they have in common: signal types, account sizes or segments, solution areas, or timing within the month. Tell me what this actually supports and what would be over-reading a small sample. I am trying to work out whether I am triaging deliberately or running out of time in a predictable way, so be direct if the pattern suggests the latter.
activities.expectedOutput: Groupings of unactioned signals by type, account profile, solution area and timing, with an honest statement of what the sample does and does not support.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE marks each signal as declined or missed before anything else. They are identical in any system and completely different in meaning, and only the person who was there knows which is which.
activities.requiredContext: Your unactioned and expired signals with type, account and solution area; your own record of which you declined deliberately versus never reached.
activitySteps: 1. Pull your unactioned and expired signals from Sales Accelerator or your own records.
2. Mark each one as either a deliberate decline or one you never reached. Only you can tell these apart, and the whole exercise depends on it.
3. Paste the list into the prompt where it asks, then run it.
4. Look for the grouping that surprises you. The ones you expected are already priced in.
5. If the pattern is about timing rather than account quality, the fix is your week rather than your judgement. Take one change to your territory health discussion.
activities.whyThisMatters: Everyone lets signals go. The question is whether you are choosing which ones, and the answer is usually visible in a pattern nobody has looked at.

activities.name: Be told a signal is expiring instead of finding out
activities.description: Set a standing watch on the signal queue so the ones approaching expiry surface without anyone going to look.
activities.prompt: Watch my signal queue and tell me, on a schedule I set, which signals are approaching expiry, which have moved since the last check, and which have gone quiet after an initial response. Rank by how close they are to expiring and how warm the account looked. Carry forward what you told me last time so I can see what I acted on and what I let go.
activities.expectedOutput: A standing watch on the signal queue reporting what is close to expiry and what has moved since the last check, rather than a one-time list.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE decides which expiring signals are worth the contact. A queue ranked by expiry date tells you what runs out first, not what is worth pursuing, and working the queue in date order is how the good accounts get the least attention.
activities.requiredContext: Access to your signal queue, the expiry window that applies to your motion, and the cadence you want to be told on.
activitySteps: 1. Set the cadence to match how fast your queue turns over, not how often you would like to look.
2. Say what counts as approaching expiry for your motion.
3. Ask it to report movement since the last check rather than the whole queue.
4. Check the first run before you trust the second.
5. After two weeks, look at what you consistently let go and decide whether that is a judgment or a capacity problem.
activities.whyThisMatters: A signal you find on the day it expires is a signal you have already lost. Being told earlier is the whole difference.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Signals arrive faster than anyone can work them, and the ones you never reach expire without telling you. This session is about being deliberate over which ones you drop.
keyTalkingPoints: A signal is an unqualified lead until confirmed, not evidence of intent. The windows are real: Contact Me signals carry a 48-hour SLA and preloaded plan priorities a 14-day SLA, with an FY27 target of at least 85 percent of TPP and Sales Accelerator signals actioned. A signal you consciously declined and a signal you never reached look identical in the data and are completely different in practice. Facilitator note: Sales Home is in preview, has only been enabled for individual contributors rather than managers, and its outreach drafting is English only, so some of the room may be working in Sales Accelerator instead.
discussionQuestions: How many signals are sitting in your queue right now that you have not looked at?
When you let a signal go, is that usually a decision or an accident?
What would have to be true for you to confidently ignore a signal?
suggestedTransitions: Move from the triaged queue to the one signal each person will action and the ones they will explicitly close.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Close by naming the signal each person will action and at least one they are deliberately closing with a reason recorded.
preparationChecklist: Before the session: open Sales Home or Sales Accelerator and bring your current signal queue, including anything already overdue.
facilitatorQuestions: Which signal in your queue is closest to expiring and why has it not been touched?
What do you actually know about the account behind it?
Which of your open plan priorities are you never realistically going to work?
listenFor: Listen for queues sorted by interest rather than by clock, for signals treated as intent rather than as unqualified leads, for outreach planned to contacts who are not in MSX, and for priorities being carried indefinitely because nobody wants to close them.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If someone's queue is empty or inaccessible, have them work the most recent signal they let expire and reconstruct what they would have needed to act on it in time.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which signal did you find you had been avoiding rather than declining?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, action the signal closest to expiry in your queue, and close at least one priority you know you will never work, with the reason written down.
bringBackEvidence: Bring the signal you actioned, what happened, and the reason you recorded on the one you closed.

DAE-SIGNAL.keyTakeaway: A signal is an unqualified lead with a clock on it. The skill is deciding quickly which ones deserve your time, not working all of them equally.

DAE-PARTNER.roleTopicDescription: Choose what genuinely goes to a partner, package it inside the data-sharing rules, and track it through acceptance and conversion instead of assuming it is handled.
DAE-PARTNER.wiifm: A referral nobody accepted expires on its own and takes the coverage with it. This is how you find that out while you can still do something.
DAE-PARTNER.name: Hand Work to a Partner and Keep It Moving
DAE-PARTNER.description: Decide what genuinely belongs with a partner, hand it over with enough for them to act, and stay on it through the acceptance and conversion windows rather than assuming it landed.
DAE-PARTNER.todayObjective: Send one referral with what the partner actually needs, and get a clear read on where your existing referrals sit against their windows.
DAE-PARTNER.whyItMatters: Partner-led is structural in this segment rather than optional help, which means referrals that quietly expire are lost coverage you chose to give away. The difference between a partner motion that works and one that does not is almost entirely about what happens after the handoff.
DAE-PARTNER.desiredOutcome: One well-packaged referral sent, a read on your open referrals against the acceptance and conversion windows, and one stalled referral chased or closed.

secondaryAgents.name: Sales Home
secondaryAgents.shortDescription: The seller landing surface inside Sales Agent, opened from Microsoft 365 Copilot. It brings your alerts and quota attainment, your prospecting signals and your pipeline into one place, and answers questions against what MSX holds. It is in preview for SME&C sellers on MSX and is enabled for individual contributors, not managers.
secondaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Pull the real state of an opportunity out of MSX and read it back plainly: the current stage and when it last moved, the recorded next step and who owns it, the close date and what supports it, and any blocker or objection captured against the account. It works across your whole book, so you can ask which opportunities in your solution area have a named competitor recorded, which partners keep letting co-sell records lapse, or which accounts already carry a discount or non-standard term. It also drafts first-touch outreach to contacts that already exist in MSX, in English.
secondaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Use it when the question is what is on the record. Deal preparation, pressure-testing a close date, working your prospecting signals, checking the concessions already in force on an account before you negotiate, or finding the other opportunities where this same objection has already come up. Reach for it first whenever you would otherwise open MSX and click through an opportunity by hand. If Sales Home has not been turned on for you, Sales Accelerator covers the same prospecting and signal work and is where your queue lives. Sales Agent is the wider conversational surface that Sales Home sits inside, so if you are already in a Sales Agent chat you do not need to switch.
keyBenefits: Replaces the click-through: stage, next step, owner, close date and open objection come back in one answer instead of four screens in MSX. Because it reads across your whole book at once, questions that used to mean opening opportunities one at a time, such as where a competitor has shown up, which partners keep lapsing, or what you have already conceded on an account, become a single prompt. Most usefully, it shows you where the record is empty, which is normally the thing costing you the deal.

activities.name: Decide what genuinely belongs with a partner
activities.description: Work out which of your opportunities a partner would actually serve better, rather than which ones you have least time for.
activities.prompt: Here are opportunities and plan priorities I am considering routing to a partner: [paste the list, with what each involves, the account, and why I am considering routing it]. For each, help me judge whether a partner genuinely serves this better or whether I am routing it because I lack capacity. Consider what the work actually needs, whether it is the kind of deployment or solution a partner typically leads, and what the customer would experience either way. Be direct where the honest answer is that I am offloading rather than orchestrating. Do not assume routing is the right answer just because I raised it.
activities.expectedOutput: A judgement per opportunity on whether a partner genuinely serves it better or whether it is a capacity decision, with what the customer would experience either way.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE decides what to route. You remain accountable for account-level orchestration after the handoff, so routing something a partner cannot serve well does not remove the problem from you, it just delays it.
activities.requiredContext: The opportunities or plan priorities you are considering routing; what each involves; the account and any existing partner relationship; your honest reason for considering it.
activitySteps: 1. List the opportunities you are thinking about routing, with why for each.
2. Paste them into the prompt where it asks, then run it.
3. Be honest in the ones where the real reason is capacity. That is sometimes the right call, but it should be a decision rather than a story.
4. Check whether the customer has an existing relationship with a partner already. That usually settles it.
5. Pick one to route properly, and take the others off the routing list rather than leaving them ambiguous.
activities.whyThisMatters: Partner-led is structural in this segment, not overflow. Routing by capacity rather than by fit is how customers end up with a partner who was never the right answer.

agents.name: Sales Agent
agents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
agents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
agents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings sales data and actions into the flow of work, including on a phone between meetings. For renewals, work that previously meant gathering data from seven or eight portals over two to three weeks becomes a few natural language prompts, with the Deal Book assembled across more than a dozen source systems. MSX records can be created or amended from the field behind a confirmation card, so context captured after a meeting does not wait until you are back at a desk.

activities.name: Package it so the partner can actually act
activities.description: Write the referral notes a partner needs to pick the work up, keeping internal detail out of the draft from the start.
activities.prompt: I am sending a referral to an external partner. Here is what I can share: [paste ONLY the customer objective, what stage the conversation is at, what has been discussed, and what I want the partner to do. Do not paste financial figures, seat or licence counts, individual names or contact details, or anything copied out of an internal system]. Draft the referral notes from what I have given you. Write for an external audience throughout: no financial or seat-level detail, no personally identifiable information, and nothing phrased as if it came off an internal screen, even if I have accidentally included some. If what I have given you is too thin to be worth sending, say so plainly rather than padding it out.
activities.expectedOutput: Referral notes covering the customer objective, conversation stage, history and your specific ask, written for an external audience, or a plain statement that there is not enough to send.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE clears the draft, and does so personally. The model cannot audit its own output for disclosure and must not be relied on to try; what makes a detail identifying is usually account context only you hold. The real control is what you decline to paste in the first place.
activities.requiredContext: The opportunity and customer objective; what has been discussed; what you want the partner to do; your team's data-sharing rules; the named partner seller.
activitySteps: 1. Take the opportunity you decided to route.

2. Before pasting anything, remove financial figures, seat and licence counts, individual names and contact details, and anything copied from an internal screen. Keeping it out is the control; nothing downstream will reliably catch it.
3. Paste what remains into the prompt where it asks, then run it.

4. Read the draft yourself against your team's data-sharing rules. Do not treat the model as having cleared it - it cannot see what is identifying about your account and it will not tell you it is unsure.

5. Send it through Accept and Send to Partner, which creates the lead in Partner Center and notifies both the partner Referrals Admin and the named partner seller. Note the date, because the acceptance window starts now.
activities.whyThisMatters: Most referrals fail because the partner cannot tell what they are being asked to do. The rest fail because something crossed that should never have left - and by the time it is in the draft, the exposure has already happened.

activities.name: Find the referrals that are about to run out of time
activities.description: Check your open referrals against the acceptance and conversion windows before the system closes them for you.
activities.prompt: Here are my open partner referrals: [paste the list from the Partner Timeline view on each plan priority, with the date sent, whether the partner has accepted, and the date of acceptance where it happened]. The windows are 14 days for the partner to accept or decline before the lead expires, and 60 days after acceptance to qualify, convert to a co-sell opportunity, or mark it lost, after which the system marks it lost automatically. Work out from the dates which are close to either boundary, which have already passed one, and which I have not given you enough information to judge. For each one at risk, tell me whether the next move is mine or the partner's.
activities.expectedOutput: Your open referrals sorted against the acceptance and conversion windows, with those near or past a boundary named, and the next move identified as yours or the partner's.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE decides what to chase. An expiring referral is sometimes worth letting go, but that should be a choice rather than something you discover after the system has closed it.
activities.requiredContext: Your open referrals from the Partner Timeline view with dates sent and accepted; the partner sellers involved; your weekly partner meeting or PDM contact.
activitySteps: 1. Open the Partner Timeline view on your plan priorities to see where each referral stands.
2. Copy the list into the prompt where it asks, with dates sent and accepted, then run it.
3. Deal with anything inside a few days of a boundary first. After the boundary the system decides for you.
4. Separate the ones waiting on the partner from the ones waiting on you. Chasing the wrong one wastes the days you have left.
5. For anything the partner has gone quiet on, raise it at the weekly partner meeting rather than sending another email into silence.
activities.whyThisMatters: These windows close on their own. A referral that expires unaccepted and one you deliberately withdrew look identical afterwards, and only one of them was a decision.

activities.name: Look at your last few stalled referrals for a common cause
activities.description: Take a small number of referrals that went nowhere and find what they had in common, rather than attempting a portfolio review.
activities.prompt: Here are the last few referrals I sent that expired unaccepted or stalled after acceptance: [paste up to five, with the partner, the type of work, and what happened to each]. Looking only at these, tell me what they appear to have in common: the same partner, similar kinds of work, or a similar point at which they stopped. Be explicit that a handful of referrals cannot establish a trend, and tell me what I would need to look at to know whether this is a real pattern. Give me one thing worth testing rather than a diagnosis.
activities.expectedOutput: What the small set appears to have in common, an explicit caveat that a handful cannot establish a trend, and one thing worth testing next.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE decides whether the apparent pattern is real. A few referrals with the same partner may be a performance problem or may be the partner you route most to, and only you know which.
activities.requiredContext: Up to five referrals you remember stalling, with the partner, the type of work and the outcome of each; your PDM contact for partner performance issues.
activitySteps: 1. Bring up to five referrals you remember going nowhere. Five you can recall accurately beats twenty you half-remember.
2. Note the partner, the work and what happened for each.
3. Paste them into the prompt where it asks, then run it.
4. Treat whatever it finds as a hypothesis, not a finding. Five referrals cannot tell you about your territory.
5. If the same partner appears more than once, that is a PDM conversation rather than something to solve one referral at a time.
activities.whyThisMatters: It is easy to conclude that partners do not follow up. Looking hard at three or four you actually remember gets you closer to the truth than a review nobody has time to run.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Handing something to a partner feels like finishing it. The windows say otherwise, and they close whether or not anyone is watching.
keyTalkingPoints: A referral sent through Accept and Send to Partner creates a lead in Partner Center and notifies both the partner Referrals Admin and the named partner seller. The partner then has 14 days to accept or decline before the lead expires, and 60 days after accepting to qualify, convert to a co-sell opportunity or mark it lost, after which the system marks it lost automatically. Status comes back through the Partner Timeline view on the plan priority. The data-sharing rules are firm: no personally identifiable information without customer consent, no financial or seat-level detail, and no MSX screenshots or exports. After the handoff you remain accountable for account-level orchestration, so a referral that fails is still your account.
discussionQuestions: How many open referrals do you have right now, and when did you last look at them?
What do you actually send a partner when you route something?
When a referral goes quiet, what do you do?
suggestedTransitions: Move from the routing decision to the one referral each person will package properly and the one they will chase or close.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Close by naming the referral each person will send or chase, and anything they are choosing to let expire deliberately rather than by default.
preparationChecklist: Before the session: open the Partner Timeline view on your plan priorities and bring your open referrals with the dates you sent them.
facilitatorQuestions: Which of the things you are routing would a partner genuinely serve better?
What would the partner need from you that you did not send?
Which of your open referrals is closest to a window closing?
listenFor: Listen for routing driven by capacity rather than fit, for referral notes too thin for anyone to act on, for internal detail about to cross to a partner, and for referrals nobody has checked since the day they were sent.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If someone has no open referrals, work the last one they sent and reconstruct what the partner would have needed to act on it. The packaging exercise is the transferable part.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did you assume the partner already knew that you had never actually told them?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, check every open referral against its window, chase the one closest to closing, and send one new referral with notes a partner could act on without calling you.
bringBackEvidence: Bring the referral you sent, what you included, and what happened to the one you chased.

DAE-PARTNER.keyTakeaway: Handing something to a partner is not the end of your involvement. The windows run whether or not anyone is watching them, and the system closes the lead for you if nobody acts.

DAE-TERRITORY.roleTopicName: Decide Who Is Actually Covering Each Account
DAE-TERRITORY.roleTopicDescription: Segment a territory you cannot work account by account into what you cover, what a partner covers and what nobody covers, then take the uncovered part into the joint plan instead of leaving it to chance.
DAE-TERRITORY.wiifm: The accounts that lapse are almost never the ones you decided to drop. They are the ones that were never on anybody's list, and you find out at renewal.
DAE-TERRITORY.name: Plan the Territory With the Partners Who Cover It
DAE-TERRITORY.description: Decide who is genuinely covering which accounts across a territory far larger than one person can work, and build that decision into a joint plan with the partners who cover the rest.
DAE-TERRITORY.todayObjective: Produce an honest coverage read on your territory and name the accounts currently covered by nobody.
DAE-TERRITORY.whyItMatters: A territory of roughly fifty accounts cannot be covered account by account, so most of it is covered by partners or not at all. The plan is where that becomes deliberate. Left implicit, the accounts that get worked are the ones that shout, and the ones that quietly lapse were never assigned to anybody.
DAE-TERRITORY.desiredOutcome: A territory segmented by actual coverage, the uncovered accounts named, and one of them either taken on or deliberately routed to a partner.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Home
primaryAgents.shortDescription: The seller landing surface inside Sales Agent, opened from Microsoft 365 Copilot. It brings your alerts and quota attainment, your prospecting signals and your pipeline into one place, and answers questions against what MSX holds. primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Pull the real state of an opportunity out of MSX and read it back plainly: the current stage and when it last moved, the recorded next step and who owns it, the close date and what supports it, and any blocker or objection captured against the account. It works across your whole book, so you can ask which opportunities in your solution area have a named competitor recorded, which partners keep letting co-sell records lapse, or which accounts already carry a discount or non-standard term. primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Use it when the question is what is on the record. Deal preparation, pressure-testing a close date, working your prospecting signals, checking the concessions already in force on an account before you negotiate, or finding the other opportunities where this same objection has already come up. Reach for it first whenever you would otherwise open MSX and click through an opportunity by hand. If Sales Home has not been turned on for you, Sales Accelerator covers the same prospecting and signal work and is where your queue lives. Sales Agent is the wider conversational surface that Sales Home sits inside, so if you are already in a Sales Agent chat you do not need to switch.
keyBenefits: Replaces the click-through: stage, next step, owner, close date and open objection come back in one answer instead of four screens in MSX. Because it reads across your whole book at once, questions that used to mean opening opportunities one at a time, such as where a competitor has shown up, which partners keep lapsing, or what you have already conceded on an account, become a single prompt. activities.name: Split the territory into covered, partner-covered and neither
activities.description: Produce an honest three-way coverage read across the whole territory rather than a list of the accounts already front of mind.
activities.prompt: List every account in my territory and group them three ways: accounts where I have had direct activity recorded this quarter, accounts with an open partner referral or co-sell opportunity of any status, and accounts with neither. For the second group, show the referral or co-sell record and whatever status field it currently carries, without interpreting what that status means. For the third group, show the account name, its segment, any open opportunity, and the date of the most recent recorded activity of any kind.
activities.expectedOutput: A three-way coverage read across the full territory with the uncovered accounts named and counted, not estimated.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE decides what counts as coverage, and confirms partner acceptance in the Partner Timeline before counting an account as covered. The agent can see that a referral exists but not whether a partner picked it up, and an unaccepted referral is an account you have told yourself is handled.
activities.requiredContext: Your assigned territory in MSX. Your open partner referrals and their acceptance status from the Partner Timeline view.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent and paste the prompt.
2. Replace nothing - it runs against the territory already assigned to you in MSX.
3. Read the third group first and count it.
4. For every account in the second group, open the Partner Timeline view on the plan priority and confirm whether the referral was actually accepted. A sent referral is not coverage.
5. Move anything not accepted into your uncovered count.
6. Note the accounts where the most recent activity date surprises you.
activities.whyThisMatters: Most territory reads start from the accounts already in mind, which is exactly the set that is already covered. Starting from the whole list is what surfaces the accounts nobody has touched.

activities.name: Test the plan priorities that were assigned to you
activities.description: Work the preloaded plan priorities against their window and decide which ones genuinely fit the territory rather than working them in the order they arrived.
activities.prompt: Show my open plan priorities with the date each was created, the account it sits against, and any recorded activity on that account since. For each, state what the priority is asking me to do and whether anything in the account record suggests it is already underway, already lost, or still untouched. Flag any where the account has had no activity at all.
activities.expectedOutput: Plan priorities sorted by remaining window with an explicit worked-or-declined decision recorded against each.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE decides which priorities are worth the window. A priority that was generated for you is not evidence that the account is ready, and declining one deliberately is a legitimate answer that a priority left to expire silently is not.
activities.requiredContext: Your open plan priorities in MSX Plans, with their creation dates.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent and paste the prompt.
2. Check each priority against the fourteen-day window from its creation date.
3. Separate the ones that fit your territory strategy from the ones that arrived because a model scored them.
4. Decide explicitly which ones you are not going to work, and record the reason.
5. Take the one closest to expiring into an action today.
activities.whyThisMatters: Preloaded priorities carry a fourteen-day SLA and expire whether or not anyone looked. A declined priority and an ignored one are identical in the data and completely different in practice.

activities.requiredContext: Your uncovered accounts from the coverage read. The CELA rules on what may be exchanged with a partner.

agents.name: Sales Home
agents.shortDescription: The seller landing surface inside Sales Agent, opened from Microsoft 365 Copilot. It brings your alerts and quota attainment, your prospecting signals and your pipeline into one place, and answers questions against what MSX holds. It is in preview for SME&C sellers on MSX and is enabled for individual contributors, not managers.
agents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Pull the real state of an opportunity out of MSX and read it back plainly: the current stage and when it last moved, the recorded next step and who owns it, the close date and what supports it, and any blocker or objection captured against the account. It works across your whole book, so you can ask which opportunities in your solution area have a named competitor recorded, which partners keep letting co-sell records lapse, or which accounts already carry a discount or non-standard term. It also drafts first-touch outreach to contacts that already exist in MSX, in English.
agents.whenToUseIt: Use it when the question is what is on the record. Deal preparation, pressure-testing a close date, working your prospecting signals, checking the concessions already in force on an account before you negotiate, or finding the other opportunities where this same objection has already come up. Reach for it first whenever you would otherwise open MSX and click through an opportunity by hand. If Sales Home has not been turned on for you, Sales Accelerator covers the same prospecting and signal work and is where your queue lives. Sales Agent is the wider conversational surface that Sales Home sits inside, so if you are already in a Sales Agent chat you do not need to switch.
keyBenefits: Replaces the click-through: stage, next step, owner, close date and open objection come back in one answer instead of four screens in MSX. Because it reads across your whole book at once, questions that used to mean opening opportunities one at a time, such as where a competitor has shown up, which partners keep lapsing, or what you have already conceded on an account, become a single prompt. Most usefully, it shows you where the record is empty, which is normally the thing costing you the deal.

In preview for SME&C individual contributors since late July 2026; it does not replace MSX.

stepsToGetStarted: Opens Sales Agent. Sales Home is the seller surface inside it - My View for alerts and quota attainment, Prospecting for signals, account research, contacts and outreach, and Pipeline for opportunities, forecast comments, close plans and deal risks. activities.name: Build the coverage position you will defend at Territory Health
activities.description: Prepare the coverage argument for the bi-weekly review, including the part that does not look good.
activities.prompt: Using my coverage read, draft the position I will take into a territory health review: how many accounts I am working directly, how many sit with a partner and are confirmed accepted, how many are covered by neither, and what I am doing about the third group. State plainly where the coverage is thin. Identify the two questions a manager is most likely to ask about this position and what evidence would answer them.
activities.expectedOutput: A defensible coverage position with the thin areas surfaced deliberately and a specific support ask attached.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE decides which gap to raise first. Bringing your own worst number to a review is a judgement about credibility that pays off over quarters, and no analysis can make that call for you.
activities.requiredContext: Your completed coverage read. The territory health review cadence for your pod.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent and paste the prompt.
2. Check the numbers against your own coverage read rather than accepting them.
3. Decide which gap you are going to raise yourself rather than waiting to be asked.
4. Prepare the specific support ask that follows from it.
activities.whyThisMatters: The bi-weekly territory health review runs with the full v-team present. The coverage position is going to be discussed whether or not you prepared it.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A territory of roughly fifty accounts cannot be worked account by account, which means most of it is covered by a partner or by nobody. This session is about finding out which.
keyTalkingPoints: The territory plan is the primary planning construct in this segment, and individual account plans still sit underneath it for Unified and MACC customers. Territory Planning in MSX Plans is shipped and operational, and Partner Center is the partner-facing surface alongside it. Preloaded plan priorities carry a fourteen-day SLA, with an FY27 target of at least eighty-five percent of TPP and Sales Accelerator signals actioned. Facilitator note: coverage model is a property of the account rather than of the seller, so a single territory will usually span Unified, non-Unified and partner-led accounts at the same time.
discussionQuestions: How many accounts are in your territory, and how many did you touch last quarter?
Of the ones you did not touch, how many is a partner genuinely working?
Who would notice if one of your accounts stopped being covered by anyone?
suggestedTransitions: Move from the coverage read to the specific uncovered accounts, then to what each person will do about one of them.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Close by having each person name the number of accounts they believe are covered by nobody, and one they are going to act on.
preparationChecklist: Before the session: open your territory in MSX Plans and bring your account list, including the accounts you have not touched this quarter.
facilitatorQuestions: Which accounts in your territory are you genuinely working, and which are you assuming somebody else has?
What evidence do you have that the partner is actually working the ones you handed over?
Which account would you be most embarrassed to discover nobody has contacted?
listenFor: Listen for coverage assumed from a referral being sent rather than accepted, for partner coverage claimed without evidence from the Partner Timeline, for territory reads built from memory rather than from the plan, and for the uncovered set being described as small without anyone having counted it.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If someone cannot reach MSX Plans, have them work from their account list and reconstruct the coverage read from what they know, which usually exposes the gap faster anyway.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which account did you assume was covered until you looked?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, produce a coverage read on your full territory and take one uncovered account either onto your own list or into a partner conversation.
bringBackEvidence: Bring the count of uncovered accounts you found and what you did with one of them.

DAE-TERRITORY.keyTakeaway: Coverage is a decision whether or not you make it. An account nobody named is an account nobody is working.

DAE-ORIENT.roleTopicName: Frontier Accelerator Orientation for Digital Account Executives
DAE-ORIENT.roleTopicDescription: Introduce the eight-session huddle motion, where AI reduces the preparation and triage load across a territory of roughly fifty accounts, which tools may appear, and what to bring back each week.
DAE-ORIENT.wiifm: You are not being asked to learn another tool. You are being asked to get time back from triage and preparation across a territory nobody could work account by account.
DAE-ORIENT.name: Frontier Accelerator Orientation
DAE-ORIENT.description: Introduces the motion, the huddle format, the AI tools in scope, and what team members are expected to try between sessions.

roles.description: Manages strategic enterprise accounts with complex multi-stakeholder deals and long sales cycles.

roles.description: Owns the technical strategy and solution roadmap for enterprise accounts.

roles.name: Commercial Executive

roles.name: Solution Engineer

roles.name: Solution Sales Professional
roles.description: Drives solution-specific opportunities by shaping vision and leading value-based conversations.

DAE-ORIENT.todayObjective: Understand how the DAE huddle path runs and where the human checkpoints protect territory, partner and deal judgement.
DAE-ORIENT.whyItMatters: Eight weeks of huddles only works if everyone understands what is being asked, what good participation looks like, and where human judgment stays non-negotiable.
DAE-ORIENT.desiredOutcome: DAEs know how the motion works, which tools may show up, and what to try before the next session.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Eight sessions, each built around one part of the job rather than one tool. This first one is about what is being asked of you and what is not.
keyTalkingPoints: The motion is about better workflow with human judgement kept explicit, not tool adoption for its own sake. Every activity names a human checkpoint - the judgement that does not get delegated. The DAE path covers territory, signals, conversations, deals, partner handoff, renewals and portfolio health. Facilitator note: Sales Agent is not available in GCC or DoD environments, and Sales Home is in preview, individual-contributor only and English only, so the room may be working in different surfaces.
discussionQuestions: Where does your week actually go, and how much of it is preparation and triage?
What have you already tried with AI, and what happened?
What would you want back if you got two hours a week?
suggestedTransitions: Move from the general discussion to the one thing each person will try before the next session.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Close by having each person name the account they will run the baseline task against, so it is specific before they leave.
preparationChecklist: Before the session: no preparation needed. Bring one recent example of something that took longer than it should have.
facilitatorQuestions: What is the part of the job that does not scale to fifty accounts?
Where would you not want AI involved at all?
What would make you distrust an output?
listenFor: Listen for expectations that the tools will do the judging, for scepticism worth taking seriously rather than arguing with, and for anyone describing a workflow that is already broken without AI.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the group is quiet, ask what they did last week that they would not want to do again.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which part of your week would you most like to stop doing manually?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, open Sales Agent and ask it to summarize one account in your territory that you have not looked at this quarter. Note one thing it told you that you did not know, and one thing it got wrong or could not answer.
bringBackEvidence: Bring the account you tried it on, the thing you did not know, and the thing it got wrong. The failure is the more useful half.

DAE-ORIENT.keyTakeaway: The point of the motion is better workflow with human judgment kept explicit, not tool adoption for its own sake.

DAE-CONV.roleTopicName: Prepare a Frontier Conversation Without a Week of Research
DAE-CONV.roleTopicDescription: Prepare a customer conversation that moves a decision when the account is one of roughly fifty and the preparation time available is measured in minutes rather than days.
DAE-CONV.wiifm: At this account load the honest choice is usually between a generic conversation and no conversation. This is how preparation becomes fast enough to happen.
DAE-CONV.name: Prepare and Lead a Customer Conversation
DAE-CONV.description: Prepare for the conversation that moves the decision, anticipate what will be asked, and lead it with evidence.

DAE-CONV.todayObjective: Prepare one customer conversation to a standard you could not reach manually in the time you actually have.

DAE-CONV.desiredOutcome: A prepared conversation with a stated outcome, the likely objection anticipated, and the evidence ready.

It is in preview for SME&C sellers on MSX and is enabled for individual contributors, not managers.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Pull the real state of an opportunity out of MSX and read it back plainly: the current stage and when it last moved, the recorded next step and who owns it, the close date and what supports it, and any blocker or objection captured against the account. It works across your whole book, so you can ask which opportunities in your solution area have a named competitor recorded, which partners keep letting co-sell records lapse, or which accounts already carry a discount or non-standard term. It also drafts first-touch outreach to contacts that already exist in MSX, in English.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Use it when the question is what is on the record. Deal preparation, pressure-testing a close date, working your prospecting signals, checking the concessions already in force on an account before you negotiate, or finding the other opportunities where this same objection has already come up. Reach for it first whenever you would otherwise open MSX and click through an opportunity by hand. If Sales Home has not been turned on for you, Sales Accelerator covers the same prospecting and signal work and is where your queue lives. Sales Agent is the wider conversational surface that Sales Home sits inside, so if you are already in a Sales Agent chat you do not need to switch.
keyBenefits: Replaces the click-through: stage, next step, owner, close date and open objection come back in one answer instead of four screens in MSX. Because it reads across your whole book at once, questions that used to mean opening opportunities one at a time, such as where a competitor has shown up, which partners keep lapsing, or what you have already conceded on an account, become a single prompt. Most usefully, it shows you where the record is empty, which is normally the thing costing you the deal.

activities.name: Find out who is already in this account
activities.description: Establish who holds the relationship before preparing, because at this account load it is often not you.
activities.prompt: For [account name], show me who is already engaged: every recorded contact and when they were last spoken to, which Microsoft roles have recorded activity, any partner referral or co-sell record attached, and any open support or delivery interaction. Then summarize the products and workloads in place, open opportunities and their stage, and the agreement dates on record. List what is missing as questions rather than filling it.
activities.expectedOutput: A picture of who already holds the relationship, alongside the account facts and the open questions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE decides whether to walk into this alone. At roughly fifty accounts the relationship often sits with a partner or another role, and arriving without them turns a useful conversation into one the customer has to repeat.
activities.requiredContext: One upcoming customer conversation and the account it concerns. The Partner Timeline view if a referral exists.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent and paste the prompt with your account.
2. Read the who-is-engaged section first. If a partner or another role holds the relationship, your conversation is a different conversation.
3. For any partner involvement, check the Partner Timeline view for what has actually happened.
4. Decide whether you should be preparing alone or with whoever already has the relationship.
activities.whyThisMatters: In a partner-led segment the person the customer already trusts is frequently not you. Finding that out before the meeting is cheaper than finding out during it.

activities.name: Work out what this customer has already been told
activities.description: Find the history that will shape the conversation, including commitments made by people who are no longer involved.
activities.prompt: For [account name], I am proposing [describe what you are proposing]. Show me the relevant history: what has been bought and when, what was deployed and whether it was used, any support issue raised and how it ended, opportunities that were opened and lost and the reason recorded, and any commitment logged against the account. Based only on that record, what is this customer likely to raise? For each, state what in the history suggests it. Do not invent customer sentiment that is not in the record.
activities.expectedOutput: The account history most likely to shape the conversation, with the specific objection it implies.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE decides which history still matters to this customer. Territories change hands and a commitment made two sellers ago is still a commitment to the customer, while a support issue that looks severe in the record may have been forgotten entirely.
activities.requiredContext: Your intended proposal and the account. The account's purchase, deployment, support and lost-opportunity history.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent, paste the prompt, and replace both bracketed sections._x000D_
2. Read the lost opportunities and closed support issues first - that is where the resistance usually comes from._x000D_
3. Check whether any commitment in the record was made by someone who has since left the account._x000D_
4. Prepare for the one piece of history most likely to come up.
activities.whyThisMatters: At this account load you are often inheriting a history you were not present for. The customer remembers it and will assume you do too.
activities.prerequisiteActivityName: Find out who is already in this account

activities.name: Name the ask and the fallback ask
activities.description: Define what decision you want out of the conversation and what you will settle for, before you are in it.
activities.prompt: For my conversation with [account name], I want [describe the outcome you want]. Help me sharpen this into a primary ask that names a specific decision and owner, and a fallback ask that is genuinely different rather than a smaller version of the same request. For each, state what the customer would need to believe to agree to it.
activities.expectedOutput: A primary ask naming a specific decision and owner, and a genuinely distinct fallback ask.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE judges whether the fallback is genuinely different. A fallback that concedes on the same axis gives the customer one decision to decline rather than two to choose between, and only the person who knows the relationship can tell whether the second ask is real.
activities.requiredContext: Your intended outcome for the conversation and the account it concerns.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent and paste the prompt with your account and intended outcome.
2. Test whether the fallback concedes on a different axis or just asks for less.
3. If it is just a smaller version, write a different one yourself.
4. Decide which you are opening with.
activities.whyThisMatters: A conversation without a defined ask produces a good discussion and no decision, which at this account load means you will not get back to it for a month.
activities.prerequisiteActivityName: Find out who is already in this account

activities.name: Write a follow-up that works when a partner is also in the motion
activities.description: Record what was decided so that everyone involved, including a partner, can act on it without asking you.
activities.prompt: Draft a follow-up for my conversation with [account name]. Here is what happened: [paste your notes]. Structure it as what was decided, what was agreed as a next step with an owner and a date, and what remains open. Where a step belongs to someone other than me, name the role rather than assuming I will do it. Keep strictly to what was said - do not promote a discussion into a decision or add commitments that were not made. Produce a customer-facing version and a short internal note; keep commercial detail out of the customer version.
activities.expectedOutput: A customer-facing follow-up and a separate internal note, with steps owned by role rather than defaulting to you.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE confirms each recorded decision was actually taken, and checks what goes to the customer separately from what goes internally, before either is sent. When Sales Agent offers to write the update, the confirmation card is the last moment before your reading of the conversation becomes the account's official version of it.
activities.requiredContext: Your notes from the conversation. Whether a partner or another role owns any next step.
activitySteps: 1. Write your rough notes first, before opening anything._x000D_
2. Open Sales Agent, paste the prompt, and replace [account name] and [paste your notes]._x000D_
3. Check every commitment against what was genuinely said._x000D_
4. Check the customer-facing version for anything commercial that should only be internal._x000D_
5. If a partner owns a next step, send them the internal note only after checking it against the CELA rules._x000D_
6. Send it, then ask Sales Agent to record what changed on the opportunity - a forecast comment or a revised close date. It will show a confirmation card before writing anything._x000D_
7. Read the card before confirming. On a phone between meetings this is the step most easily tapped through, and it is the only check there is.
activities.whyThisMatters: When a partner or another role owns the next step, a follow-up written only for you produces a decision nobody actions. Naming the owner is what makes it move.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: The preparation that makes a customer conversation land is the first thing dropped when the calendar fills. This session is about making it cheap enough to survive.
keyTalkingPoints: Discovery intent is the same as Enterprise - the Frontier Conversation and BOAT framing still apply - but the time available per account is materially different. Contacts must already exist in MSX before outreach can be drafted against them. Sales Home outreach drafting is English only and in preview. Facilitator note: the execution ask this year includes a large volume of C-suite Frontier conversations, so the pressure is toward more conversations, which makes preparation quality the thing at risk.
discussionQuestions: How long do you actually spend preparing for a customer conversation?
What do you skip when you are short of time?
When did generic preparation last cost you a meeting?
suggestedTransitions: Move from the prepared brief to the specific ask each person will make.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Close by having each person state the outcome they want and the fallback ask if they do not get it.
preparationChecklist: Before the session: bring one customer conversation you have coming up in the next fortnight.
facilitatorQuestions: What is the decision you actually want out of this conversation?
What will they push back on, and do you have an answer?
What are you assuming about who is in the room?
listenFor: Listen for conversations with no stated outcome, for objections nobody has thought about until now, for stakeholder assumptions drawn from a title rather than a behaviour, and for preparation that produces talking points rather than a decision.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If nobody has an upcoming conversation, use the last one that did not land and reconstruct what preparation would have changed it.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What did you find you were assuming about this customer?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, prepare one customer conversation this way and note whether the objection you anticipated was the one that came up.
bringBackEvidence: Bring what you prepared, what actually happened, and where the preparation was wrong.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Home
primaryAgents.shortDescription: The seller landing surface inside Sales Agent, opened from Microsoft 365 Copilot. It brings your alerts and quota attainment, your prospecting signals and your pipeline into one place, and answers questions against what MSX holds. It is in preview for SME&C sellers on MSX and is enabled for individual contributors, not managers.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Pull the real state of an opportunity out of MSX and read it back plainly: the current stage and when it last moved, the recorded next step and who owns it, the close date and what supports it, and any blocker or objection captured against the account. It works across your whole book, so you can ask which opportunities in your solution area have a named competitor recorded, which partners keep letting co-sell records lapse, or which accounts already carry a discount or non-standard term. It also drafts first-touch outreach to contacts that already exist in MSX, in English.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Use it when the question is what is on the record. Deal preparation, pressure-testing a close date, working your prospecting signals, checking the concessions already in force on an account before you negotiate, or finding the other opportunities where this same objection has already come up. Reach for it first whenever you would otherwise open MSX and click through an opportunity by hand. If Sales Home has not been turned on for you, Sales Accelerator covers the same prospecting and signal work and is where your queue lives. Sales Agent is the wider conversational surface that Sales Home sits inside, so if you are already in a Sales Agent chat you do not need to switch.
keyBenefits: Replaces the click-through: stage, next step, owner, close date and open objection come back in one answer instead of four screens in MSX. Because it reads across your whole book at once, questions that used to mean opening opportunities one at a time, such as where a competitor has shown up, which partners keep lapsing, or what you have already conceded on an account, become a single prompt. Most usefully, it shows you where the record is empty, which is normally the thing costing you the deal.

activities.name: Separate what you can see from what you are assuming
activities.description: Establish the real state of a deal where part of the motion is happening outside your systems.
activities.prompt: For [opportunity name or ID], show what the MSX record actually contains: the current stage and when it last moved, the recorded next step and its owner, the close date and whether it has been changed, any co-sell or referral record attached and its recorded status, and the date of the most recent activity of any kind. Do not infer progress from the stage, and do not describe what the partner is doing - the record shows only what has been entered here. Where a field is empty, say so rather than filling it.
activities.expectedOutput: A deal state showing what the record evidences, what is empty, and what is known only from conversation.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE decides what counts as known. A stage in MSX records what someone last entered rather than what is happening, and when a partner is transacting, the most important movement is the movement you cannot see from here.
activities.requiredContext: One live deal, ideally one where a partner is involved in the transaction.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent and paste the prompt with your opportunity.
2. List separately what you know from a conversation rather than from the record.
3. The co-sell record shows what exists in MSX, not what the partner is doing. For that, open the Partner Timeline view or Partner Center.
4. Mark anything you have not confirmed in the last fortnight as unknown.
activities.whyThisMatters: A deal a partner is closing looks the same in our systems as a deal that has quietly died. The distinction has to be made deliberately.

activities.name: Name the next decision and who actually makes it
activities.description: Find the specific decision that moves the deal and the person with authority to make it.
activities.prompt: For [opportunity name or ID], based on the current stage and what is recorded, what is the next decision this deal needs?
