Distinguish decisions the customer makes from decisions Microsoft or a partner makes. Where the record does not identify a decision maker, say so.
activities.expectedOutput: The next decision named with its owner, what they need, and whether it sits with the customer, Microsoft or the partner.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE judges whether the named decision maker is real. A contact recorded as a decision maker was entered by someone at some point, and in a partner-led motion the person who actually decides is often someone the partner knows and we do not.
activities.requiredContext: One live deal and its current stage. Any known stakeholders on the customer side.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent and paste the prompt with your opportunity.
2. Check whether the named decision maker is someone you have actually spoken to.
3. If the decision sits with a partner, work out whether you can influence it or only ask about it.
4. Define the single thing that would unblock it.
activities.whyThisMatters: Deals stall because the next decision is fuzzy rather than because it was refused. Naming it is most of the work of unsticking it.

activities.name: Prepare the specific ask for the partner
activities.description: Turn the gaps in your view into one clear question the partner can answer quickly.
activities.prompt: I have a deal at [account name] where a partner is involved in the transaction. Here is what I know and what I do not: [paste your deal state]. Help me draft a short, specific message to the partner asking for what I actually need to know. Keep it to two or three questions. Do not include internal commercial detail, seat counts, spend figures or anything that reads as an export from our systems.
activities.expectedOutput: A short partner message asking two or three specific questions, checked against the data-sharing boundary before sending.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE owns what crosses to the partner and checks it before sending. Even when instructed to exclude commercial detail, a model may reintroduce it while making the message clearer, and the sender is the only control on that.
activities.requiredContext: Your deal state showing what is unknown. The CELA rules on what may be shared with a partner.
activitySteps: 1. Take your deal state from the first activity._x000D_
2. Open Sales Agent, paste the prompt, and replace both bracketed sections._x000D_
3. Check the draft against the CELA rules - no personal data, no seat or spend detail, nothing resembling an export._x000D_
4. Cut it to the two questions you most need answered._x000D_
5. Send it through your normal partner channel.
activities.whyThisMatters: Partners answer specific questions quickly and general status requests slowly, if at all. The difference is whether you did the thinking before asking.

activities.name: Test the close date against the evidence
activities.description: Work out whether the date in the system is a forecast or a hope.
activities.prompt: For [opportunity name or ID], the close date is currently recorded as [date]. Based on the stage, the recorded next step, the decision still outstanding and the most recent activity, what would have to happen between now and that date for it to close on time? List the steps in sequence with realistic elapsed time for each. If a partner referral or co-sell motion is part of this deal, account for the fourteen days a partner has to accept a referral before it expires and the sixty days to convert it before it is automatically marked lost. Identify the first step that has not started.
activities.expectedOutput: A backward plan from the close date showing the first step not yet started and whether the date is achievable.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE owns the close date and changes it when the arithmetic does not support it. A date that survives because nobody recalculated it is the most common cause of a forecast miss, and the confirmation card is worth reading precisely because moving a date is easy now - the ease is the risk, not the safeguard.
activities.requiredContext: One live deal with a close date on record. Its current stage and outstanding decisions.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent and paste the prompt with your opportunity and its close date._x000D_
2. Compare the total elapsed time against the days remaining._x000D_
3. If a referral is in flight, check its actual age in the Partner Timeline rather than assuming the window is still open._x000D_
4. Decide whether to move the date or compress a step, and do one of them._x000D_
5. If you are moving it, ask Sales Agent to change the close date in the same chat. It will show a confirmation card with the old and new values before writing._x000D_
6. Check the new date is the one your own arithmetic produced rather than the one that felt comfortable, then confirm.
activities.whyThisMatters: Close dates get set optimistically and then inherited. Working backwards from the date is the fastest way to find out it was never going to happen.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: When a partner is transacting the deal, your view of it is partial by design. This session is about working out what you actually know.
keyTalkingPoints: Partner-led is structural in this segment rather than optional, and the partner frequently closes. Partner-side activity is not visible in MSX; it returns through the Partner Timeline view or Partner Center. A deal progressing well through a partner and a deal that has quietly died look identical from inside our systems. Facilitator note: this is the session where the difference between what the record shows and what is actually happening matters most, and the honest answer is often that nobody has asked the partner recently.
discussionQuestions: How do you currently find out what a partner is doing on a deal?
When did you last discover a deal was dead well after it died?
What do you do differently when the partner is closing?
suggestedTransitions: Move from the deal read to the one ask each person will take to the partner or the customer.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Close by naming the ask each person is making and who they are making it of.
preparationChecklist: Before the session: bring one live deal where a partner is involved in the transaction.
facilitatorQuestions: What do you genuinely know about this deal versus what you are inferring from the record?
When did you last speak to the partner about it?
What is the next decision, and who actually makes it?
listenFor: Listen for partner activity inferred from MSX stage rather than confirmed, for next decisions owned by nobody, for deals described as progressing on the strength of an old conversation, and for reluctance to chase a partner in case it looks like distrust.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If nobody has a partner-involved deal live, use the most recent one that closed and reconstruct where visibility was lost.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: What were you assuming was happening that you have not actually confirmed?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, establish the real state of one partner-involved deal by asking the partner directly, and record what you learned that the system did not show.
bringBackEvidence: Bring the gap between what MSX said and what the partner said.

DAE-RENEW.wiifm: Renewals arrive in a queue and get worked in date order, which is almost never risk order. The one that surprises you was always visible earlier.

activities.name: Sort the renewal book by risk instead of by date

activities.expectedOutput: A renewal book sorted by the evidence a customer would raise at renewal, rather than by date.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE decides what constitutes renewal risk in this book. An unresolved issue may have been forgotten and a deployment gap may be deliberate, and only someone who knows the account can tell a real risk from a data artefact.
activities.requiredContext: Your accounts with agreement or renewal dates in the next twelve months.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent and paste the prompt.

4. Reorder your book on that basis rather than on date.
activities.whyThisMatters: A book worked in date order means the renewal you reach last is the one you had most time to fix. Sorting by risk inverts that.

activities.name: Work out which renewals you can actually evidence
activities.description: Test across the renewal book which accounts you could defend with evidence today, because you will not have time to build it for all of them.
activities.prompt: For these accounts approaching renewal [list your at-risk renewals], show for each what the record evidences about value delivered: workloads deployed and when, usage recorded where it exists, support issues raised and resolved, and any milestone or success activity logged. Group them into accounts where a value story could be told from the record today, accounts where something is missing, and accounts where there is essentially nothing. Do not fill gaps with inference.
activities.expectedOutput: The renewal book grouped by whether a value story can be evidenced today, with the accounts that cannot be evidenced identified first.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE decides where to spend the evidence-building effort. At this book size you cannot build a value story for every renewal, so choosing which ones go undefended is a real decision that gets made either deliberately or by running out of time.
activities.requiredContext: Your at-risk renewal accounts. Their deployment, usage and support history as recorded.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent, paste the prompt, and replace the bracketed list with your at-risk renewals._x000D_
2. Read the third group first - those are the ones that need work now, whatever their dates._x000D_
3. For the middle group, identify the single missing piece._x000D_
4. Decide which accounts you can realistically build evidence for before their dates, and which you cannot.
activities.whyThisMatters: Value evidence takes time to assemble and the book is larger than the time available. Knowing which renewals you cannot defend is as useful as knowing which you can.
activities.prerequisiteActivityName: Sort the renewal book by risk instead of by date

activities.name: Find the expansion already inside the renewal
activities.description: Test whether the account has an obvious next step that is easier to land than a new pursuit.
activities.prompt: For [account name], based on what is deployed and what is not, identify the expansion steps that would be a natural progression from the current estate. Consider specifically: security and compliance add-ons where the customer is on a base tier, moves from standalone products to suite licensing, upgrades from a lower to a higher suite tier, and Copilot attach where the underlying suite is already in place. For each, state what in the current estate makes it a logical next step and what would need to be true for the customer to want it. Do not present these as qualified opportunities and do not assume eligibility or pricing.
activities.expectedOutput: Expansion hypotheses grounded in the deployed estate, with the most plausible one tested against customer context.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE decides which expansion is real, and routes eligibility and pricing to the Commercial Executive rather than assuming them. A logical next product is not a wanted one, and the record does not know what the customer has budgeted or been burned by before.
activities.requiredContext: One renewal account and its current deployed estate.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent and paste the prompt with your renewal account.
2. Discard anything that does not build on something already deployed.
3. Test the most plausible one against what you know of the customer's plans.
4. Decide whether it belongs in the renewal conversation or as a separate pursuit.
activities.whyThisMatters: Expansion inside a healthy renewal is materially easier than a new pursuit, and the evidence for it is usually already sitting in what the customer has deployed.
activities.prerequisiteActivityName: Work out which renewals you can actually evidence

activities.name: Work out what the Commercial Executive needs from you
activities.description: Prepare the renewal handoff so the commercial work can start before the structure is already fixed.
activities.prompt: For [account name] with a renewal approaching, assemble what a Commercial Executive would need to begin: the current agreement type and end date, what is deployed against it, the expansion or reduction being contemplated, any known customer constraint, and the timeline pressure. Identify what is missing that only I can supply.
activities.expectedOutput: A renewal briefing the CE can act on, with the seller-only gaps filled before it is sent.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE decides when to bring the CE in, and does it before the commercial shape is already fixed. Commercial Executives own enrollment mechanics and renewal structure, and engaging them after a structure has been discussed with the customer removes most of the options they would have had.
activities.requiredContext: One renewal account approaching its date. Its agreement type and deployed estate.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent and paste the prompt with your renewal account.
2. Fill the gaps that only you can answer before sending anything.
3. Send it to your CE with the date you need a view by.
4. Do not wait for the renewal quarter to do this.
activities.whyThisMatters: The CE can change the shape of a renewal if they are involved while it is still a question. Once a structure has been floated with the customer, they are correcting rather than designing.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Renewals arrive in date order and almost never in risk order. This session is about resorting them.
keyTalkingPoints: The renewal motion here runs across a book of agreements rather than a single account, on a long workback from the renewal date rather than a conversation in the final quarter. Mid-term expansion is often the more available move: security add-ons, moves from standalone to suite licensing, tier upgrades and Copilot attach. Commercial Executive owns enrollment mechanics, commercial strategy and the renewal structure itself. Facilitator note: at this book size, the renewal that goes wrong is usually one nobody looked at rather than one somebody misjudged.
discussionQuestions: How do you decide which renewal to work first?
How far ahead do you actually start?
Where has an expansion been easier than a new opportunity?
suggestedTransitions: Move from the risk-sorted book to the one renewal each person will act on.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Close by naming the renewal each person is acting on and why it moved up the list.
preparationChecklist: Before the session: bring your renewal book with dates, or as much of it as you can see.
facilitatorQuestions: Which renewal are you working because it is next rather than because it is at risk?
What evidence of delivered value exists for the one closest to its date?
Where is there an expansion sitting inside a renewal you were treating defensively?
listenFor: Listen for books worked in date order, for value assumed rather than evidenced, for expansion framed as a separate pursuit rather than part of the renewal, and for CE engaged after the structure is already fixed.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If renewal data is not accessible, work from the last renewal that was harder than expected and identify when it first became visible.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which renewal were you going to reach too late?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, sort your renewal book by risk rather than date, act on the highest-risk one, and test one expansion hypothesis inside a renewal you were treating defensively.
bringBackEvidence: Bring the renewal that moved up your list and what you did about it.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Home
primaryAgents.shortDescription: The seller landing surface inside Sales Agent, opened from Microsoft 365 Copilot. It brings your alerts and quota attainment, your prospecting signals and your pipeline into one place, and answers questions against what MSX holds. It is in preview for SME&C sellers on MSX and is enabled for individual contributors, not managers.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Pull the real state of an opportunity out of MSX and read it back plainly: the current stage and when it last moved, the recorded next step and who owns it, the close date and what supports it, and any blocker or objection captured against the account. It works across your whole book, so you can ask which opportunities in your solution area have a named competitor recorded, which partners keep letting co-sell records lapse, or which accounts already carry a discount or non-standard term. It also drafts first-touch outreach to contacts that already exist in MSX, in English.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Use it when the question is what is on the record. Deal preparation, pressure-testing a close date, working your prospecting signals, checking the concessions already in force on an account before you negotiate, or finding the other opportunities where this same objection has already come up. Reach for it first whenever you would otherwise open MSX and click through an opportunity by hand. If Sales Home has not been turned on for you, Sales Accelerator covers the same prospecting and signal work and is where your queue lives. Sales Agent is the wider conversational surface that Sales Home sits inside, so if you are already in a Sales Agent chat you do not need to switch.
keyBenefits: Replaces the click-through: stage, next step, owner, close date and open objection come back in one answer instead of four screens in MSX. Because it reads across your whole book at once, questions that used to mean opening opportunities one at a time, such as where a competitor has shown up, which partners keep lapsing, or what you have already conceded on an account, become a single prompt. Most usefully, it shows you where the record is empty, which is normally the thing costing you the deal.

activities.name: Find the accounts that changed direction
activities.description: Look for movement rather than for low numbers, and cross-check it against the consumption view the agent cannot see.
activities.prompt: Across my accounts, show me the ones where something has changed recently: opportunities that moved stage or stalled, support issues opened, activity that stopped, or renewal dates approaching without recent contact. For each, show what changed and when. Do not rank them by size or attempt to score their health; just show me what moved.
activities.expectedOutput: The accounts where something changed in MSX, cross-referenced by hand against consumption movement, with the changes described rather than scored.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE distinguishes a change that matters from a change that is normal for that account, and does the consumption comparison manually because the agent cannot. A quiet quarter is a warning at one customer and the usual pattern at another, and nothing in the record encodes which.
activities.requiredContext: Your assigned accounts and their recent activity, opportunity and support records. Separately, whatever consumption or usage view you have access to - the agent cannot reach it.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent and paste the prompt._x000D_
2. Read the accounts that went quiet before the ones with visible problems._x000D_
3. Open your consumption or usage view separately. The agent cannot compute month-on-month consumption movement, so this comparison is yours to make._x000D_
4. Mark any account where consumption has moved by roughly a quarter in either direction - that scale of swing is the segment's standing trigger for a look._x000D_
5. Separate movement with an obvious explanation from movement without one.
activities.whyThisMatters: A low number tells you where an account already is. A change tells you where it is going, and that is the one you can still do something about.

activities.name: Find out whether it is one account or a pattern
activities.description: Test whether the movement you found is specific to that account or showing up across several, because the two need completely different responses.
activities.prompt: Several of my accounts are showing [describe the movement you found]. For the accounts in my portfolio, show me which others have the same characteristics: the same workloads, a similar deployment stage, the same recorded issue type, or the same agreement structure. For each match, show what it has in common and what is different. Do not conclude that a shared characteristic is a shared cause.
activities.expectedOutput: A read on whether the movement is isolated or shared across accounts, with the common characteristics identified.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE judges whether a shared characteristic is a shared cause. Accounts on the same workload can decline for entirely unrelated reasons, and treating a coincidence as a pattern sends an escalation that wastes everyone's time.
activities.requiredContext: The movement you identified across your portfolio. Your full account list with workloads and agreement structures.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent, paste the prompt, and replace [describe the movement you found]._x000D_
2. If several accounts share the pattern, this is not an account problem and escalating it one account at a time will not fix it._x000D_
3. If it is genuinely isolated, treat it as a single-account intervention._x000D_
4. Decide which of the two you are dealing with before choosing what to do.
activities.whyThisMatters: At this portfolio size the same problem usually shows up in several accounts at once. Handling it one account at a time is the single most expensive mistake available here.

activities.name: Decide what is yours and route the rest
activities.description: Separate the accounts where your own involvement changes the outcome from the ones that need somebody else.
activities.prompt: I have these accounts showing problems: [list the accounts and what is happening at each]. For each, show the coverage arrangement on record - whether there is a Unified support agreement, an assigned customer success or technical role, or an active partner relationship. Using that, help me think through who would own the intervention each account needs and what evidence they would need to act without coming back to me. Where the coverage arrangement is not recorded, say so rather than guessing.
activities.expectedOutput: Each account routed according to its actual coverage arrangement, with the evidence the receiving role requires.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE decides which account is genuinely theirs, using the coverage arrangement rather than instinct. Coverage is a property of the account rather than of you, so the same problem at two accounts routes to two different owners, and taking on the technical intervention yourself means the accounts that needed you go unattended.
activities.requiredContext: The accounts showing movement and your read on each. The coverage arrangement on record for each account.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent, paste the prompt, and replace the bracketed list with your accounts._x000D_
2. Read the coverage arrangement first - it determines who owns the intervention before the problem does._x000D_
3. Unified accounts route differently from non-Unified, and partner-led accounts differently again._x000D_
4. Assemble the evidence the receiving role needs, then route._x000D_
5. Record that you routed it, so it is not silently yours again in a month.
activities.whyThisMatters: At this account load the failure mode is not missing a problem. It is taking on a problem that belonged to somebody else and losing the week.

activities.name: Check whether last month's interventions actually worked
activities.description: Close the loop on the accounts you already acted on, because nothing in the working week will tell you whether anything changed.
activities.prompt: For these accounts where I intervened recently [list the accounts and what you did], show what has happened since: any change in opportunity stage, new or resolved support issues, activity recorded and by whom, and whether the next step logged at the time was completed. For each, show what has moved and what has not. Do not judge whether the intervention succeeded.
activities.expectedOutput: A read on which recent interventions produced movement and which did not, with a decision on each of the latter.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE decides whether an intervention has failed or simply needs longer. The record shows movement rather than progress, and an intervention that quietly did nothing will stay on your list indefinitely unless someone decides to stop.
activities.requiredContext: The accounts you intervened at recently and what you did. The activity and opportunity record since.
activitySteps: 1. Write down what you actually did at each account and when, before opening anything._x000D_
2. Open Sales Agent, paste the prompt, and replace the bracketed list._x000D_
3. Look for interventions where nothing has moved at all - those either failed or never started._x000D_
4. Decide for each whether to escalate, try something different, or accept it and stop spending time there.
activities.whyThisMatters: Interventions get started and rarely get checked. At this account load the ones that silently failed are indistinguishable from the ones still in flight until somebody looks.

activities.name: Let the territory tell you when it moves
activities.description: Set a standing check across the territory so a change reaches you when it happens rather than at the next review.
activities.prompt: Set up a recurring weekly check across the accounts in my territory. Each week, show me where an opportunity has changed stage or close date, where a new signal or plan priority has arrived and how long it has before it expires, where a renewal date has moved inside twelve months, and where a partner referral has changed status. For each, state what changed and what the record does not tell us. Remember what you reported before so you can separate what is new from what I have already seen.
activities.expectedOutput: A weekly view of territory movement separating new changes from previously reported ones, with expiring items surfaced.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The DAE decides which movement needs action this week. A territory of this size generates change constantly and most of it is noise, so the judgment is which change alters what you were going to do anyway.
activities.requiredContext: Your territory of accounts. The signal, opportunity and renewal sources you can reach.
activities.bestFitJob: Let the territory tell you when it moves
activitySteps: 1. Open Scout and confirm which signal, opportunity and referral sources it can reach for your territory.
2. Run the prompt and set the cadence to land before your own pipeline review.
3. The first run reports everything. Read it once, then tune it to movement rather than inventory.
4. Act on expiring signals first - they are the only items on the list with a deadline you cannot negotiate.
activities.whyThisMatters: At this territory size nothing surfaces on its own. The choice is between a standing check and finding out at the review, and the review is always too late for the signals that expire.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: You will not notice an account going wrong by looking at it, because you are not looking at most of them. You notice by watching what changed.
keyTalkingPoints: Portfolio health in this segment is about direction of travel across many accounts rather than deep inspection of a few. Consumption movement of roughly a quarter up or down month on month is the kind of change worth a look. Coverage model is a property of the account rather than of the seller, so one portfolio spans Unified, non-Unified and partner-led accounts with different support behind each. Facilitator note: the technical intervention usually belongs to the D-CSA or a partner, so the DAE judgement here is about noticing and routing rather than fixing.
discussionQuestions: How would you currently find out an account was in trouble?
Which accounts have you not thought about this quarter?
What is the earliest signal you have ever caught?
suggestedTransitions: Move from the movement read to the one account each person acts on and the ones they route.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Close by naming the account each person is acting on and at least one they are deliberately routing elsewhere.
preparationChecklist: Before the session: bring your account list and any consumption or usage view you have access to.
facilitatorQuestions: Which accounts changed direction rather than simply being low?
What is the explanation, and is it a real one or a guess?
Which of these is genuinely yours to act on?
listenFor: Listen for low absolute numbers mistaken for decline, for movement explained by assumption rather than evidence, for accounts being taken on personally that belong with the D-CSA or a partner, and for the uncovered portion going unmentioned.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If consumption data is unavailable, use recorded activity as the movement signal and work from the accounts that have gone quiet.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which account had changed direction without you noticing?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, identify the accounts in your portfolio that changed direction, act on one, and route one to the D-CSA or a partner with the evidence attached.
bringBackEvidence: Bring the movement you found, what caused it, and what you did.

SMEC-CE-ORIENT.roleTopicName: Frontier Accelerator Orientation for Commercial Executives in SME&C
SMEC-CE-ORIENT.roleTopicDescription: Introduce the eight-session motion, where AI reduces the commercial research and preparation load across a book of agreements rather than a handful, and what to bring back each week.
SMEC-CE-ORIENT.wiifm: Commercial work here is spread across far more agreements than anyone can inspect individually, and much of it transacts through a partner. This is about getting the research time back.
SMEC-CE-ORIENT.name: Frontier Accelerator Orientation
SMEC-CE-ORIENT.description: Introduces the motion, the huddle format, the AI tools in scope, and what team members are expected to try between sessions.

roles.description: Drives solution-specific opportunities by shaping vision and leading value-based conversations.

SMEC-CE-ORIENT.todayObjective: Understand how the CE path runs in this segment and where the human checkpoints protect commercial and policy judgement.
SMEC-CE-ORIENT.whyItMatters: Eight weeks of huddles only works if everyone understands what is being asked, what good participation looks like, and where human judgment stays non-negotiable.
SMEC-CE-ORIENT.desiredOutcome: CEs know how the motion works, which tools may show up, and what to try before the next session.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Eight sessions, each built around one part of the commercial job rather than one tool. This first one is about what is being asked and what is not.
keyTalkingPoints: The motion is about better workflow with human judgement kept explicit, not tool adoption. Every activity names a human checkpoint - the judgement that is not delegated. In this segment the commercial role covers enrollments, renewals and commercial strategy across a large book, and a substantial share transacts through a partner rather than directly. Facilitator note: Sales Agent is not available in GCC or DoD, and policy and licensing interpretation always routes to the authoritative owner rather than to any agent.
discussionQuestions: How much of your week goes to assembling commercial context rather than deciding anything with it?
How many agreements are you responsible for, and how many did you look at last month?
What have you already tried with AI, and what happened?
suggestedTransitions: Move from the discussion to the one thing each person will try before the next session.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Close by having each person name the account they will run the baseline task against.
preparationChecklist: Before the session: no preparation needed. Bring one piece of commercial work that took longer than it should have.
facilitatorQuestions: What is the commercial work that does not scale to a book this size?
Where would you never want an AI answer?
What would make you distrust an output?
listenFor: Listen for expectations that an agent will interpret policy, for scepticism worth taking seriously, and for workflows that are already broken without AI.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If the group is quiet, ask what commercial question they answered most often last month.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which part of your commercial week would you most like to stop doing manually?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, open Sales Agent and ask it to summarize the agreement position on one account in your book you have not looked at this quarter. Note one thing you did not know and one thing it got wrong.
bringBackEvidence: Bring the account, the thing you did not know, and the thing it got wrong. The failure is the more useful half.

SMEC-CE-ORIENT.keyTakeaway: The point of the motion is better workflow with human judgment kept explicit, not tool adoption for its own sake.

SMEC-CE-RENEW.wiifm: By the time a renewal is in its final quarter, most of the commercial options have closed. The value you add is almost entirely a function of when you arrive.

Covers pre-meeting account summaries, fast pipeline lookups, and updating MSX from the field behind a confirmation card. Current as of August 2026.

primaryAgents.whenNotToUseIt: Do not treat Deal Agent as a separate agent to select; it is a skill inside Sales Chat. Do not rely on it alone for complex negotiations or sensitive disclosures, and do not bypass the legal approval chain for material amendments. Do not treat a first response as final on a complex deal; re-run and verify against current data. Do not use it for work outside the CRM such as decks, emails, and documents; that is Cowork. When it offers a confirmation card before creating or changing an MSX record, read what it is about to write rather than confirming by reflex - nothing is committed until you tap, and that tap is the only check on it.
stepsToGetStarted: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams or Outlook, or install the Microsoft 365 Copilot app on your phone. Use the agent picker to find and select Sales; no separate install is required. Start a new chat with a deal prompt such as: List my upcoming renewals this quarter. Deal Agent triggers automatically. Keep one chat thread per deal so the context stays clean. On mobile, name the account or opportunity explicitly - Sales Agent is sharpest when pointed at a specific record. MCAPS Help is built in, so you can also ask how to complete an MSX task.

activities.name: Sort the book by where commercial options are still open
activities.description: Order a renewal book by how much commercial room remains rather than by how soon each date arrives.
activities.prompt: List the accounts in my book with an agreement end date in the next eighteen months. For each, show the date, the agreement type, the products and quantities on the agreement, whether a partner is associated with the account, and the most recent recorded activity. Group them by how far out the date is: more than twelve months, six to twelve months, and under six months.
activities.expectedOutput: A renewal book grouped by remaining commercial room, with the partner-transacted agreements marked.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CE decides where commercial room genuinely remains. Time to the date is a proxy for optionality rather than the thing itself, and an agreement eighteen months out whose customer has already committed a budget is more closed than one at six months that has not.
activities.requiredContext: Your book of agreements with end dates and agreement types. Partner association where it exists.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent and paste the prompt.
2. Work the first group before the third. The renewals over twelve months out are the only ones where structure is genuinely still open.
3. Mark which are partner-transacted - your role differs on those.
4. Pick the earliest-dated agreement in the first group that carries real value.
activities.whyThisMatters: Almost all the commercial value a CE adds depends on arriving while the structure is still a question. A book worked in date order guarantees arriving last at the ones with most room.

agents.name: Sales Agent
agents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
agents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
agents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings sales data and actions into the flow of work, including on a phone between meetings. For renewals, work that previously meant gathering data from seven or eight portals over two to three weeks becomes a few natural language prompts, with the Deal Book assembled across more than a dozen source systems. MSX records can be created or amended from the field behind a confirmation card, so context captured after a meeting does not wait until you are back at a desk.

activities.name: Establish what the agreement actually says versus what is happening
activities.description: Compare the commercial commitment on paper against the deployed reality, because the gap is the renewal conversation.
activities.prompt: For [account name], show the current agreement position: the agreement type and end date, the products and quantities committed, what is actually deployed against them, and any amendment or exception recorded. Highlight where deployed quantities differ from committed quantities in either direction. Do not interpret licensing entitlement or eligibility - show what is recorded and flag what needs an authoritative answer.
activities.expectedOutput: The committed position against the deployed position, with the gaps identified and the entitlement questions routed rather than answered.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CE owns the commercial interpretation and routes entitlement and eligibility to the authoritative source rather than accepting a generated reading. A confidently wrong licensing answer is discovered at signature, and by then it has been built on.
activities.requiredContext: One renewal account and its agreement record. Access to the authoritative licensing source for anything about entitlement.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent, paste the prompt, and replace [account name] with your renewal._x000D_
2. Read the over-deployment and under-deployment separately - they are opposite commercial problems._x000D_
3. Route anything touching entitlement, eligibility or pricing to the authoritative source. Do not accept the agent's reading of it._x000D_
4. Decide which gap changes the renewal structure.
activities.whyThisMatters: Under-deployment is a renewal risk and over-deployment is a compliance exposure. Both are visible long before the date, and neither surfaces on its own.

activities.name: Work out what changes when the partner holds the renewal
activities.description: Establish where your influence sits on a renewal a partner will transact, and what they need from you.
activities.prompt: For [account name], a renewal where a partner transacts, show what is visible from here: the agreement position, the partner associated with the account, any co-sell or referral record, and the recorded activity on both sides. Then help me separate the parts of this renewal I can decide, the parts I can only recommend, and the parts I will not see at all. Do not describe partner-side activity - the record shows only what has been entered in MSX.
activities.expectedOutput: The renewal separated into what you decide, what you recommend, and what is not visible to you, with one partner need identified.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CE decides what to escalate to the partner conversation rather than working around it. In CSP the partner owns the customer commercial relationship, and a CE who tries to run the renewal directly damages the relationship that will actually deliver it.
activities.requiredContext: One partner-transacted renewal. The partner associated with it. Partner Center or the Partner Timeline view for partner-side status.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent, paste the prompt, and replace [account name] with a partner-transacted renewal._x000D_
2. Treat the third category as the important one - what you will not see is what will surprise you._x000D_
3. Check the Partner Timeline view or Partner Center for the partner-side picture; the agent cannot reach it._x000D_
4. Decide the one thing the partner needs from you that they do not currently have.
activities.whyThisMatters: Treating a partner-transacted renewal like a direct one produces advice nobody asked for and a partner who stops sharing information. The boundary is worth being explicit about.

activities.name: Check whether the agreement allows a mid-term change at all
activities.description: Establish what this agreement type actually permits before anyone takes an expansion idea to the customer.
activities.prompt: For [account name], show the agreement type, its start and end dates, any anniversary or true-up mechanism recorded, the amendment history, and any co-term arrangement. Based only on what is recorded, describe what changes have previously been made mid-term on this agreement and when in its cycle they happened. Do not state what the agreement type permits in general and do not assess eligibility - I will confirm that with the authoritative source.
activities.expectedOutput: A read on whether a mid-term change is mechanically available on this agreement, evidenced by amendment history and confirmed with the authoritative source.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CE confirms the mechanism with the authoritative source before anyone acts on it. Prior amendment history is evidence rather than permission, and an expansion promised on an agreement that cannot carry it until renewal costs credibility with the account team and the customer at once.
activities.requiredContext: One account with an agreement in place, including amendment history and any true-up or anniversary mechanism. The authoritative source for what the agreement type permits.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent, paste the prompt, and replace [account name] with the account._x000D_
2. Read the amendment history first. What has already been done mid-term is the most reliable evidence of what can be._x000D_
3. Confirm the mechanism with the authoritative licensing source before telling anyone it is available. The agent does not reliably know which amendments an agreement type allows._x000D_
4. Give the account team a clear yes, no, or confirm-first, with the date it would need to happen by.
activities.whyThisMatters: Account teams generate expansion ideas continuously. The commercial question is not whether the idea is good but whether the paper allows it now, and that answer is worth days if it arrives early.

activities.name: Check the renewals that arrived without you
activities.description: Work through renewal opportunities created automatically and decide which of them describe a renewal you would stand behind.
activities.prompt: Show me the renewal opportunities in my book that were created automatically rather than by me, using their creation date between [start date] and [end date]. For each, show the account, the recorded value and currency, the close date, the enrollment or agreement record it was built from, the product or SKU lines attached, and the forecast category currently set. Report what is recorded. Do not assess whether any value, date or line is correct.
activities.expectedOutput: Auto-created renewals reviewed with account, value, close date and product lines each confirmed or corrected, forecast category set by the CE, anything that should not exist routed rather than edited, and one flagged difference between what arrived and what was expected.
activities.humanCheckpoint: For each auto-created renewal the CE decides one of three things: accept it as it stands, correct it against the agreement, or reject it as a renewal that should not be in the book. The CE also decides whether and when to set a forecast category, which is the point at which the record becomes a commitment rather than a suggestion.
activities.requiredContext: Your renewal book for the period, including opportunities you did not create. The underlying agreement or enrollment record for anything you intend to correct.
activities.bestFitJob: Own the renewals that arrived in pipeline without you
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent and paste the prompt with your start and end dates.
2. For each opportunity, validate four things yourself against the agreement and the customer: the account it landed on, the value and currency, the close date, and the product or SKU lines attached.
3. Correct what is wrong and add what is missing - contacts, and any required field - before the opportunity progresses to the next stage.
4. Where the renewal should not exist at all, say so and route it rather than editing it into something plausible.
5. Set the forecast category yourself. The record existing is not the same as you committing to it.
6. Pick the one where what arrived differs most from what you would have entered, and work out why. That gap is the thing worth discussing.
activities.whyThisMatters: A renewal that appears in pipeline without anyone deciding it belongs there is a forecast entry nobody has stood behind. The work is no longer creating the record, it is deciding whether to own it.
activities.prerequisiteActivityName: Sort the book by where commercial options are still open

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: A renewal you reach in its final quarter is a renewal you can process. A renewal you reach a year out is one you can shape.
keyTalkingPoints: The renewal motion here is an always-on workback across a book rather than a sequence of individual events, and it starts well over a year ahead of the date. Both EA and CSP agreements are in scope and they behave differently: in CSP the partner holds the transaction and often leads the later stages. Mid-term expansion is frequently the more available move - security add-ons, moves from standalone to suite licensing, tier upgrades and Copilot attach. Facilitator note: the CE owns enrollments, renewals and commercial strategy, and eligibility or pricing interpretation still routes to the authoritative source rather than to an agent.
discussionQuestions: How far ahead do you actually start on a renewal?
Which of your renewals are transacted by a partner rather than by us?
When did a renewal last reach you too late to shape?
suggestedTransitions: Move from the sorted book to the one renewal each person will start a workback on.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Close by naming the renewal each person is starting a workback on and how far out it is.
preparationChecklist: Before the session: bring your renewal book with dates and agreement types, or as much of it as you can see.
facilitatorQuestions: Which renewal in your book still has commercial options open, and which has effectively closed?
Where does a partner hold the transaction, and what does that change about your role?
What would you need to know a year out that you currently learn three months out?
listenFor: Listen for books worked in date order, for CSP renewals treated the same as direct ones, for expansion framed as a separate pursuit, and for the assumption that arriving earlier is not possible.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If renewal data is not accessible, use the last renewal that arrived too late and work out when it first became visible.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which renewal did you assume you had time on?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, sort your renewal book by where commercial options are still open rather than by date, and start a workback on the earliest one that matters.
bringBackEvidence: Bring the renewal you started on and what you found was already decided.

primaryAgents.name: Sales Home
primaryAgents.shortDescription: The seller landing surface inside Sales Agent, opened from Microsoft 365 Copilot. It brings your alerts and quota attainment, your prospecting signals and your pipeline into one place, and answers questions against what MSX holds. It is in preview for SME&C sellers on MSX and is enabled for individual contributors, not managers.
primaryAgents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Pull the real state of an opportunity out of MSX and read it back plainly: the current stage and when it last moved, the recorded next step and who owns it, the close date and what supports it, and any blocker or objection captured against the account. It works across your whole book, so you can ask which opportunities in your solution area have a named competitor recorded, which partners keep letting co-sell records lapse, or which accounts already carry a discount or non-standard term. It also drafts first-touch outreach to contacts that already exist in MSX, in English.
primaryAgents.whenToUseIt: Use it when the question is what is on the record. Deal preparation, pressure-testing a close date, working your prospecting signals, checking the concessions already in force on an account before you negotiate, or finding the other opportunities where this same objection has already come up. Reach for it first whenever you would otherwise open MSX and click through an opportunity by hand. If Sales Home has not been turned on for you, Sales Accelerator covers the same prospecting and signal work and is where your queue lives. Sales Agent is the wider conversational surface that Sales Home sits inside, so if you are already in a Sales Agent chat you do not need to switch.
keyBenefits: Replaces the click-through: stage, next step, owner, close date and open objection come back in one answer instead of four screens in MSX. Because it reads across your whole book at once, questions that used to mean opening opportunities one at a time, such as where a competitor has shown up, which partners keep lapsing, or what you have already conceded on an account, become a single prompt. Most usefully, it shows you where the record is empty, which is normally the thing costing you the deal.

activities.name: Separate what you decide from what you recommend
activities.description: Map your actual authority on a deal a partner will transact, before spending effort on the parts you do not hold.
activities.prompt: For [opportunity name or ID], where a partner will transact, show the deal position recorded in MSX: stage, products, quantities, any co-sell or referral record, the account's existing agreements, and the partner associated. Then help me categorize the commercial elements into ones Microsoft decides, ones the partner decides, and ones the customer decides. Where the record does not make ownership clear, say so rather than assuming.
activities.expectedOutput: Commercial elements separated by who actually decides them, with the one element worth your effort identified.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CE decides where their input actually changes the outcome. Advising on an element the partner owns is effort that produces friction rather than a different deal, and only someone who knows the partner relationship can tell which is which.
activities.requiredContext: One live deal a partner will transact. The account's existing agreements. The partner associated with it.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent and paste the prompt with your opportunity.
2. Look hardest at the middle category - that is where effort gets wasted.
3. For anything you decide, confirm it against current approved guidance rather than the agent's reading.
4. Pick the single element where your input changes the outcome most.
activities.whyThisMatters: The most common way commercial effort is wasted in this segment is spending it on decisions that belong to somebody else. Mapping authority first is the cheapest work available.

activities.name: Compare the structures the partner could actually sell
activities.description: Test commercial options against what is transactable through this route rather than what would be optimal directly.
activities.prompt: For [opportunity name or ID], the customer needs [describe the commercial requirement]. Based on the account's existing agreements and what is recorded, lay out the commercial structures that could meet it. For each, state what it requires from the customer, what it requires from the partner, and what has to be true about the existing agreement for it to work. Flag anything that depends on policy, eligibility or pricing that I need to confirm with the authoritative source rather than assume.
activities.expectedOutput: Commercial structures compared on what is actually transactable through this route, with the policy questions routed rather than assumed.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CE judges what the partner can genuinely transact, and confirms every policy and eligibility question with the authoritative owner before comparing options. A structure that is commercially elegant and cannot be sold through this route is a recommendation that wastes a cycle for everyone.
activities.requiredContext: One live deal and the customer's commercial requirement. The account's existing agreements. The authoritative source for policy, eligibility and pricing.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent, paste the prompt, and replace both bracketed sections._x000D_
2. Discard any structure the partner cannot transact through their route, whatever its merits._x000D_
3. Route every policy, eligibility and pricing flag to the authoritative owner before comparing._x000D_
4. Choose the structure that is best among the transactable ones, not best in the abstract.
activities.whyThisMatters: Structures are usually compared on commercial merit and then discovered to be untransactable through the route in play. Applying that filter first changes which option wins.

activities.name: Give the partner what makes the right structure easy to sell
activities.description: Turn your commercial recommendation into something the partner can actually use with the customer.
activities.prompt: I want a partner to sell [describe the commercial structure] to [account name]. Draft a short explanation they could use with the customer: what the structure is, what it gives the customer, what it requires from them, and the two questions the customer is most likely to ask. Write it for an audience outside Microsoft. Do not include internal margin or cost detail, seat counts, spend figures, personal data, or anything that reads as an export from our systems.
activities.expectedOutput: A partner-usable explanation of the structure, checked against the data-sharing boundary before it leaves Microsoft.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CE owns what crosses to the partner and checks the draft against the data rules before sending. A model asked to make a commercial structure persuasive will reach for the numbers that make it persuasive, and the sender is the only control on that.
activities.requiredContext: Your recommended commercial structure and the account. The CELA rules on partner data exchange.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent, paste the prompt, and replace both bracketed sections._x000D_
2. Check the draft against the CELA rules before it goes anywhere: no personal data, no seat or spend detail, nothing resembling an export._x000D_
3. Read it as the partner would - if it only makes sense with your explanation attached, it is not finished._x000D_
4. Send it through your normal partner channel.
activities.whyThisMatters: A structure a partner cannot explain will not be sold, whatever its merits. Enablement is the actual lever when somebody else transacts.

activities.name: Check what this deal sets up for the next one
activities.description: Test whether a structure that works here creates an expectation you will inherit across the book.
activities.prompt: I am considering [describe the commercial structure] for [account name]. Show me other accounts in my book with a similar agreement type, size band, or product mix. For each, show the current agreement position and whether anything similar has already been done. Do not conclude that a similar account implies a similar outcome; just show me where the comparison would be drawn.
activities.expectedOutput: The accounts where this structure would set a comparison, with an explicit decision on whether it is repeatable.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CE judges whether a structure is a precedent or an exception, and records the reason. In a segment with many similar customers and shared partners, an exception granted once and undocumented becomes the expected baseline within a quarter.
activities.requiredContext: Your proposed commercial structure and account. Your wider book of agreements.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent and paste the prompt with your structure and account.
2. Look for accounts where a partner would notice the difference, not just the customer.
3. Decide whether you would be comfortable doing this for all of them.
4. If not, work out what makes this account genuinely different and write it down.
activities.whyThisMatters: Enterprise deals are large enough to be treated individually. Here the customers are numerous and similar, and partners talk, so a one-off shape propagates quickly.

agents.name: Sales Home
agents.shortDescription: The seller landing surface inside Sales Agent, opened from Microsoft 365 Copilot. It brings your alerts and quota attainment, your prospecting signals and your pipeline into one place, and answers questions against what MSX holds. It is in preview for SME&C sellers on MSX and is enabled for individual contributors, not managers.
agents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Pull the real state of an opportunity out of MSX and read it back plainly: the current stage and when it last moved, the recorded next step and who owns it, the close date and what supports it, and any blocker or objection captured against the account. It works across your whole book, so you can ask which opportunities in your solution area have a named competitor recorded, which partners keep letting co-sell records lapse, or which accounts already carry a discount or non-standard term. It also drafts first-touch outreach to contacts that already exist in MSX, in English.
agents.whenToUseIt: Use it when the question is what is on the record. Deal preparation, pressure-testing a close date, working your prospecting signals, checking the concessions already in force on an account before you negotiate, or finding the other opportunities where this same objection has already come up. Reach for it first whenever you would otherwise open MSX and click through an opportunity by hand. If Sales Home has not been turned on for you, Sales Accelerator covers the same prospecting and signal work and is where your queue lives. Sales Agent is the wider conversational surface that Sales Home sits inside, so if you are already in a Sales Agent chat you do not need to switch.
keyBenefits: Replaces the click-through: stage, next step, owner, close date and open objection come back in one answer instead of four screens in MSX. Because it reads across your whole book at once, questions that used to mean opening opportunities one at a time, such as where a competitor has shown up, which partners keep lapsing, or what you have already conceded on an account, become a single prompt. Most usefully, it shows you where the record is empty, which is normally the thing costing you the deal.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: On a partner-transacted deal you advise on a commercial relationship you do not own. This session is about being precise on which levers are actually yours.
keyTalkingPoints: A substantial share of commercial motion in this segment runs through CSP, where the partner sells and invoices. That changes the CE role from executing a structure to shaping one somebody else will execute, and the partner frequently leads the later stages. CELA rules govern what can be exchanged with a partner: personal data, MSX screenshots and exports, and financial or seat-level detail are off-limits. Facilitator note: the useful distinction in the room is between advice, enablement and execution - most frustration here comes from trying to execute through someone else.
discussionQuestions: On your last partner-transacted deal, what did you actually control?
Where have you given commercial advice that the partner then did not follow?
What can you not share with a partner, and where does that hurt?
suggestedTransitions: Move from the lever analysis to the one piece of enablement each person will prepare.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Close by naming the enablement each person is preparing and who it is for.
preparationChecklist: Before the session: bring one live deal where a partner will transact.
facilitatorQuestions: Which parts of this structure can you decide, and which can you only recommend?
What would make the partner choose a different structure than the one you would pick?
What does the partner need from you that you have not given them?
listenFor: Listen for advice framed as instruction, for structures assumed to be adopted because they were recommended, for partner exchange that would breach the data rules, and for frustration that is really about a boundary rather than a partner.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If nobody has a live partner-transacted deal, use the most recent one and identify where the structure diverged from the recommendation.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Where were you trying to execute through somebody else?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, separate what you control from what you influence on one partner-transacted deal, and give the partner one specific thing that makes the right structure easier for them to sell.
bringBackEvidence: Bring what you prepared and whether the partner used it.

activities.name: Scan the book for the gap between bought and used
activities.description: Find where deployed reality has drifted from the commercial commitment, across the whole book rather than one account.
activities.prompt: Across the accounts in my book, show each agreement with its type, end date, the products and quantities committed, and what is deployed against them. Identify the accounts where deployed quantities are materially below what was committed, and separately the accounts where they are above. Show the size of the difference for each. Do not interpret entitlement or compliance.
activities.expectedOutput: The book split into under-deployed and over-deployed accounts with the size of each gap, ranked against agreement dates.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CE decides which gaps are commercially real. A deployment gap can be a customer who over-bought deliberately, a rollout that is simply slow, or a genuine problem, and the record does not distinguish them. Compliance-shaped findings route to the authoritative owner rather than being resolved here.
activities.requiredContext: Your book of agreements with committed quantities. Whatever deployment or usage view you have access to.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent and paste the prompt.
2. Treat the two lists as different problems: under-deployment is a renewal risk, over-deployment is an exposure.
3. Route anything that looks like a compliance question to the authoritative owner rather than resolving it.
4. Rank by the size of the difference against how close the agreement date is.
activities.whyThisMatters: At this book size nobody finds a deployment gap by looking at an account. It is found by scanning for the difference, and it is the single most reliable early signal of a renewal in trouble.

agents.name: Sales Agent
agents.shortDescription: Conversational sales agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, reached through the agent picker as Sales, on desktop and on mobile through the Microsoft 365 Copilot app as well as in Teams and Outlook. Deal Agent runs as a skill inside Sales Chat and triggers automatically when you ask about a renewal or a deal.
agents.whatItHelpsYouDo: Search, synthesize, and act on sales data, and support repeatable execution-focused sales workflows. Through the Deal Agent skill it also runs enterprise renewals end to end: deal discovery and history, Deal Book generation, EA quotes and proposals, amendments, pre-approvals, and licensing questions, traversing more than a dozen source systems from a natural language prompt.
agents.whenToUseIt: Account, opportunity, pipeline, meeting preparation, CRM updates, and configured sales actions. Also on mobile immediately before or after a customer meeting: account summaries, pipeline and usage health, decision makers on an opportunity, list price lookups, and updating MSX in the moment by creating an opportunity, changing a close date or adding a forecast comment. For renewals and deals, ask about enrollments, renewal agreements, agreement summaries, license estate, Azure consumption against commitment, Deal Books, EA quotes, proposals, amendments, and pre-approvals. EA and MCA-E renewals are the primary motion. Lead with an identifier such as a TPID, agreement number, or enrollment number; specific prompts return real deal data and vague prompts return generic answers.
keyBenefits: Brings sales data and actions into the flow of work, including on a phone between meetings. For renewals, work that previously meant gathering data from seven or eight portals over two to three weeks becomes a few natural language prompts, with the Deal Book assembled across more than a dozen source systems. MSX records can be created or amended from the field behind a confirmation card, so context captured after a meeting does not wait until you are back at a desk.

activities.name: Find the exception you have granted more than once
activities.description: Identify where a one-off concession has quietly become the standing expectation across the book.
activities.prompt: Across my accounts, show the agreements carrying a recorded amendment, exception or non-standard term. For each, show what the variation is, when it was recorded, the agreement type and the account size band. Group them by the type of variation and show how many accounts each group covers. Do not judge whether any variation was appropriate.
activities.expectedOutput: Recorded variations grouped by type with the count of accounts affected, and a decision on the largest group.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CE decides whether a repeated variation should be standardised, stopped, or escalated as evidence that policy no longer matches practice. That is a judgement about commercial consistency across a book, and no individual deal review will ever surface it.
activities.requiredContext: Your book of agreements including recorded amendments, exceptions and non-standard terms.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent and paste the prompt.
2. Look at the group sizes before the individual accounts.
3. Any variation appearing across several accounts has stopped being an exception, whatever it is called.
4. Decide whether to standardise it, stop granting it, or escalate that the policy no longer matches practice.
activities.whyThisMatters: Exceptions are granted one deal at a time and reviewed one deal at a time, which is exactly why nobody notices when one has become the default.

activities.name: Tell an unattended agreement apart from a partner-covered one
activities.description: Work out whether an agreement with no activity behind it is genuinely abandoned or is being worked somewhere you cannot see.
activities.prompt: For the accounts in my book showing no recorded Microsoft activity in the last six months, show for each whether a partner is associated with the account, whether any co-sell or referral record exists and what status it carries, and whether any partner-attributed transaction has been recorded against the agreement. Group them into accounts with an active partner association, accounts with a lapsed or closed partner record, and accounts with no partner involvement recorded at all. Do not describe what any partner is currently doing.
activities.expectedOutput: Silent agreements separated into partner-covered, partner-lapsed, and genuinely unattended, with the third group escalated.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CE decides which silence is real. An agreement being worked well by a partner and an agreement nobody has touched look identical from inside our systems, and treating the first as neglect damages the partner relationship that is actually delivering the account.
activities.requiredContext: Your book of agreements with activity history. Partner association and co-sell records. Partner Center or the Partner Timeline view for partner-side status.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent and paste the prompt._x000D_
2. The third group is the genuinely unattended one. Start there._x000D_
3. For the first two groups, check Partner Center or the Partner Timeline view - the agent cannot see partner-side activity, so silence here means nothing on its own._x000D_
4. For anything in the second group, the partner record lapsing is the signal, not the silence._x000D_
5. Raise the third group with the account team this week.
activities.whyThisMatters: Silence is the most misread signal in a partner-led segment. The distinction that matters is not how quiet an account is but whether anyone else is in it.

activities.name: Build the case that policy no longer matches practice
activities.description: Turn a repeated exception into evidence a policy owner can act on.
activities.prompt: I have found that [describe the variation] appears across [number] accounts in my book. Help me structure this as a case for a policy owner: what the variation is, how consistently it appears, what commercial pressure appears to be driving it, and what the options are. Frame the options as questions for the policy owner rather than recommendations. Do not state what the policy should be or assert that any variation is permitted.
activities.expectedOutput: A structured case for the policy owner with the pattern evidenced and the options framed as questions.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CE presents evidence and does not propose the policy. A field observation carries weight precisely because it is an observation, and a case that arrives with the answer already written is read as advocacy and discounted.
activities.requiredContext: Your grouped exception finding with the account count verified. The authoritative policy owner for this variation.
activitySteps: 1. Open Sales Agent, paste the prompt, and replace the bracketed sections with your finding._x000D_
2. Check the account count yourself rather than accepting it._x000D_
3. Remove anything that reads as you deciding the policy - that is not your call and framing it that way gets it dismissed._x000D_
4. Send it to the policy owner with the evidence attached.
activities.whyThisMatters: A repeated exception is either a policy that needs changing or a practice that needs stopping. Neither gets resolved while it stays visible only to the person granting it.
activities.prerequisiteActivityName: Find the exception you have granted more than once

activities.name: Keep watching the book between reviews
activities.description: Set a standing check across the agreement book so commercial exposure surfaces before it becomes a renewal problem.
activities.prompt: Set up a recurring check across the agreements in my book that runs every two weeks. Each time, show me where an agreement end date has moved, where a new exception or amendment has been recorded, and where a renewal date has come inside the window I specify. Report only what has changed since the previous run. Do not assess commercial risk and do not recommend action.
activities.expectedOutput: A change-only view, refreshed every two weeks, of agreement dates moving, new exceptions recorded, and renewals entering the window.
activities.humanCheckpoint: The CE decides which movement is commercially material. An exception recorded on one account is administration; the same exception appearing repeatedly is a policy signal, and only someone reading across the book over time can tell which one they are watching.
activities.requiredContext: Your book of agreements. The consumption, amendment and renewal data you can reach.
activities.bestFitJob: Keep watching the book between reviews
activitySteps: 1. Open Scout and set the check running against your book of agreements.
2. Run the prompt and set it to repeat every two weeks. Commercial exposure moves more slowly than pipeline and a weekly check would mostly report nothing.
3. Read the first run in full, then read only the changes after that.
4. Decide which movements need a conversation and which are administrative.
activities.whyThisMatters: Commercial exposure in this segment accumulates quietly across many small agreements. Nobody discovers it in a single review, because no single account looks like a problem.

facilitatorGuide.sessionIntroduction: Commercial risk in this segment is small, numerous, and usually found at renewal. This session is about finding it earlier.
keyTalkingPoints: Portfolio-level commercial exposure looks different from the single-deal risk an Enterprise CE inspects: many agreements, each individually modest, where the cost is in the aggregate and in the lateness of discovery. Typical shapes include agreements approaching a date with no engagement, deployed estates that have drifted from what was purchased, and exceptions granted once that have quietly become the expected baseline. Facilitator note: policy and eligibility interpretation always routes to the authoritative owner - the work here is noticing and routing, not ruling.
discussionQuestions: How would you currently find out an agreement was going wrong?
Which of your agreements have you not looked at this quarter?
What commercial problem have you seen repeat across several accounts?
suggestedTransitions: Move from the exposure scan to the one risk each person will act on.
facilitatorGuide.wrapUpGuidance: Close by naming the risk each person is acting on and what made it the most expensive one.
preparationChecklist: Before the session: bring your agreement book and any view you have of what is deployed against it.
facilitatorQuestions: Where is the gap between what was bought and what is being used?
Which exception have you granted more than once?
Which of these is genuinely commercial rather than a delivery problem wearing commercial clothes?
listenFor: Listen for exposure estimated rather than counted, for a repeated exception not recognised as a pattern, for commercial framing applied to delivery problems, and for the largest risks going unmentioned because they are spread thin.
facilitatorGuide.fallbackGuidance: If book-level data is unavailable, work from the last commercial surprise and identify the earliest point it could have been seen.
facilitatorGuide.reflectPrompt: Which commercial risk had you been treating as somebody else's?
facilitatorGuide.commitPrompt: Before the next huddle, scan your book for commercial exposure, identify the risk that would cost most if found at renewal, and start one intervention on it.
bringBackEvidence: Bring the exposure you found and the intervention you started.

DSS-SIGNAL.roleTopicName: Judge Which Engagement Signals Are Real
DSS-SIGNAL.roleTopicDescription: Work the Highly Engaged and program signals in your solution area, separate genuine buying intent from activity, and route each one before the window closes.

DSS-SIGNAL.description: Take an inbound queue of marketing signals and plan priorities, decide fast which ones are real, and act on them inside the window rather than after it.
DSS-SIGNAL.todayObjective: Take the engagement signals in your solution area and decide, with evidence, which represent real intent and which do not.

DSS-SIGNAL.desiredOutcome: Your solution-area signals separated into real intent, needs-more-evidence and noise, with one routed and the reasoning recorded.
